Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding Citibanks contradictory investigation, repeated restriction and closure of my accounts, and its continued refusal to provide access to approximately {$34000.00} that Citi is holding in my personal deposit and brokerage accounts. This matter arose from a check issued to me from a home-equity line of credit serviced by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX I am a borrower and obligor on that HELOC. The check was issued directly to me and made payable in my name. The check was deposited into my XXXX account. XXXX later restricted and closed my accounts after allegations were apparently made by the other borrower on the HELOC. Although I provided XXXX with loan documents and evidence showing that I was a borrower and that the check had been issued to me, XXXX continued restricting my accounts and ultimately terminated its relationship with me. On or around XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX transferred approximately {$25000.00} of my funds into my personal Citibank account. Those funds remain in my Citi personal account. I also have approximately {$9000.00} in a Citi brokerage account. Therefore, Citi is currently holding approximately {$34000.00} belonging to me. Before XXXX transferred the {$25000.00}, checks that I had written from my Citi business account were returned on or around XXXX XXXX XXXX. Citi began restricting and closing my accounts because the HELOC check had been returned unpaid. However, the check was not counterfeit, forged, stolen, or issued without authorization. I participated in an approximately three-hour telephone call with a Citi fraud department supervisor . During that call, Citi conducted a three-way conversation with XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX. XXXX directly confirmed to Citi that : * The HELOC check was legitimate; * The check had been authorized and issued to me; * I was a borrower or obligor associated with the HELOC; * The check was not fraudulent or counterfeit ; and * The check was returned only because the other borrower called and froze the credit line during the time the check was being presented for payment. After receiving this confirmation from XXXX, the Citi fraud supervisor told me that he would send my accounts back for further review and reconsideration. Several weeks later, I received written correspondence from Citi indicating that my accounts were being reopened. However, when I attempted to create a username and regain access to Citis online banking system, I discovered that the accounts had been blocked again. When I contacted Citi, I was told that I would not receive online access or access to my funds until I brought my business account current. I repeatedly explained that Citi was already holding approximately {$25000.00} in my personal account and approximately {$9000.00} in my brokerage account. I requested that Citi permit me to transfer enough of those funds into my business account to satisfy or substantially reduce the negative balance. Citi refused. Citi has therefore created an impossible and coercive situation. It is holding approximately {$34000.00} of my money, preventing me from accessing or transferring that money, and simultaneously demanding that I obtain additional outside funds before it will restore access to the funds it already holds. The {$25000.00} transferred by XXXX is not being disputed as belonging to Citi. It was transferred from my XXXX account into my Citi personal account. It remains in my name and under Citis control. Nevertheless, Citi will not allow me to transfer those funds from my personal account into my business account to address the negative balance. Citi has also refused my requests to internally apply or transfer the funds itself. As a result, Citi has prevented me from using my own money to resolve the very account deficiency that Citi says is preventing access. In an effort to comply with Citis demands, I sold or pawned substantially all of my valuable personal property. I also took out an emergency loan carrying approximately XXXX percent interest compounded daily. Through these extraordinary measures, I obtained approximately {$19000.00} to provide to Citi in an attempt to bring the business account current and regain access to my accounts. Even after I obtained those funds, Citi continued refusing to allow the remaining balance to be addressed through a transfer from the approximately {$34000.00} Citi already held. I have now exhausted my available resources. I have no additional funds to provide Citi. Meanwhile, Citi continues to retain my personal and brokerage funds and refuses to permit a reasonable internal transfer. This situation has continued for nearly a month and a half. Citis actions are especially concerning because : 1. Citi directly verified with XXXX that the HELOC check was legitimate and authorized. 2. Citi was informed that the check was returned only because the other borrower froze the credit line after the check had been issued. 3. A Citi fraud supervisor advised me that the matter would be reconsidered. 4. Citi subsequently sent written correspondence stating that my accounts were being reopened. 5. Citi then blocked the accounts again without giving me a clear explanation. 6. Citi is holding approximately {$34000.00} in my personal and brokerage accounts. 7. Citi refuses to allow me to transfer those funds to my business account. 8. Citi refuses to perform the transfer itself. 9. Citi nevertheless demands additional outside funds as a condition of restoring access. 10. Citis refusal has forced me to sell valuables and incur an extraordinarily expensive emergency loan. Citi has not provided a meaningful written explanation identifying : * Why it reversed its written decision to reopen the accounts; * What new information caused the accounts to be blocked again ; * Whether Citi still claims the HELOC check was fraudulent; * Why Shellpoints direct confirmation was insufficient; * The exact amount required to bring the business account current ; * Why funds in my Citi personal and brokerage accounts can not be transferred or applied; * What legal or contractual restriction prevents an internal transfer; * What steps I must complete to obtain access to the remaining funds ; or * When Citi intends to release my undisputed money. I recognize that a bank may investigate returned checks and may decide whether to continue a customer relationship. However, Citi should not be permitted to retain approximately {$34000.00} belonging to a customer, block the customer from using those funds, refuse to internally apply the funds toward a claimed negative balance, and then demand outside money as the sole condition for access. Citis conduct appears unfair, contradictory, and abusive. Citi has placed me in a financial trap in which the bank controls more than enough money to substantially resolve the issue but refuses to either release or apply it. The continued restriction has caused severe financial harm, including : * The sale and pawning of valuable personal property; * An emergency loan carrying approximately 10 percent interest compounded daily ; * Additional debt and financing costs ; * Loss of access to approximately {$34000.00} ; * Inability to conduct ordinary personal and business transactions; * Disruption of my business operations; * Difficulty paying rent and basic living expenses; * Loss of access to my Citi brokerage funds; * Damage to my ability to maintain or establish banking relationships ; and * Severe financial and emotional distress. I respectfully request that the CFPB require Citi to take the following actions : 1. Immediately provide access to all undisputed funds in my personal deposit and brokerage accounts. 2. Permit me to transfer sufficient funds from my personal or brokerage accounts into my business account to address any legitimate negative balance. 3. Alternatively, internally apply the necessary amount toward the negative balance and release all remaining funds to me. 4. Provide a complete accounting of every Citi account associated with me, including all deposits, returned checks, debits, holds, offsets, restrictions, transfers, and balances. 5. Identify the exact amount Citi claims is necessary to bring the business account current. 6. Explain why Citi will not allow the negative balance to be resolved using funds already held in my Citi accounts. 7. Identify any legal, regulatory, or contractual prohibition that Citi believes prevents such an internal transfer. 8. Explain why Citi issued written correspondence indicating that the accounts would reopen and then blocked the accounts again. 9. Identify any new evidence Citi received after issuing the reopening correspondence. 10. Confirm the substance of the three-way call in which XXXX verified that the HELOC check was legitimate and authorized. 11. Provide the notes and records associated with the approximately three-hour call involving Citi, XXXX, and me. 12. Explain whether Citi continues to classify the transaction as fraud despite XXXX confirmation. 13. Reimburse the interest, fees, and borrowing costs arising from the emergency loan I was forced to obtain. 14. Reimburse documented losses caused by the forced sale or pawning of my property. 15. Correct or remove any inaccurate information Citi reported to XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX, credit-reporting agencies, fraud databases, or other financial institutions. 16. Confirm whether Citi communicated with XXXX, XXXX, the other HELOC borrower, or any other institution concerning my accounts. 17. Provide copies of all closure notices, reopening notices, investigation findings, account notes, fraud referrals, and nonprivileged records relied upon in restricting my accounts. 18. Immediately release any funds exceeding the legitimate amount necessary to resolve the business account balance. I have made repeated good-faith attempts to resolve this matter. I participated in an extensive fraud investigation, arranged direct verification from XXXX, provided substantial outside funds, and repeatedly proposed a reasonable internal transfer. Citi has rejected every reasonable solution while continuing to retain approximately {$34000.00} of my money. I am requesting immediate CFPB intervention because I have exhausted my personal resources and can not continue borrowing or selling property merely to satisfy Citis demand for outside funds while Citi refuses to make available the funds it already holds.

Consumer complaint narrative: In XX/XX/year>, a temporary authorization hold of 120 was placed on my PayPal Cashback Mastercard account for a transaction that was later identified as fraudulent. This transaction was only an authorization hold and was never finalized or settled. The merchant fully released and refunded the authorization, and no valid charge ever existed. Despite the transaction being both fraudulent and refunded, Synchrony Bank, the issuer of the PayPal Cashback Mastercard, incorrectly treated the authorization as a posted charge and later processed it as a disputed transaction. This occurred even though the merchant had already refunded the amount and there was no legitimate debt. As part of this improper dispute handling, Synchrony charged PayPal for the transaction. In turn, PayPal debited my PayPal balance approximately {$140.00}, leaving my PayPal account with a negative balance, even though the transaction was fraudulent, the merchant fully refunded the 120 authorization, the charge was never finalized or valid, and I do not owe this amount to either institution. At the same time, Synchrony Bank has been sending me recurring billing and past-due email notifications stating that I owe money related to this same alleged debt, including late fees and interest. However, Synchrony will not provide access to an actual billing statement. When I click the links in these emails to view the bill online, I am redirected to PayPal, where no Synchrony bill or statement is visible. I am receiving payment demands and late-fee notices for a debt that I can not view, verify, or reconcile. I have contacted both PayPal and Synchrony Bank multiple times. Each institution refuses to resolve the issue and instead directs me to the other. PayPal states the issue must be handled by Synchrony Bank, while Synchrony Bank states the issue must be handled by PayPal. As a consumer, I am being improperly charged and threatened with fees due to a failure between two financial institutions to correctly handle a fraudulent and refunded authorization and to provide required billing transparency. This is not a valid debt. I am being asked to pay money that neither PayPal nor Synchrony Bank is legally entitled to collect, and I am being assessed late fees and interest without access to a proper billing statement. I am requesting immediate removal of the negative balance from my PayPal account, immediate cessation of all billing notices, late fees, and interest related to this transaction, written confirmation that I do not owe this amount to PayPal or Synchrony Bank, assurance that this matter will not be sent to collections or reported negatively, and correction of all internal records related to this transaction. I am filing this complaint because neither PayPal nor Synchrony Bank has taken responsibility for correcting errors arising from their internal fraud, dispute, settlement, and billing processes, despite clear evidence that the transaction was fraudulent, refunded, never finalized, and never resulted in a valid charge.

I am also requesting an explanation of why I was not identified as an affected borrower for purposes of the CFPB restitution process and whether my account should be reconsidered for relief based on my servicing history. I would like a written response addressing these concerns and explaining what corrective action, if any, will be taken.

In addition, the names appearing on the paperwork were different between the two claims. I am requesting a thorough review of the denied {$120.00} claim and a detailed written explanation of why it was treated differently from the approved {$110.00} claim. I also request that Truist investigate the discrepancies involving the mailing address and the names shown on the claim documents to determine whether these errors affected the outcome of my claim. My concern is not simply that one claim was denied, but that two claims arising from the same scam, reported during the same phone call on XXXX XXXX, and supported by the same facts were handled inconsistently without a clear explanation. I respectfully disagree with KeyBanks findings and request that this complaint remain open for further review. My dispute has never been that I did not physically initiate the payment. My dispute is that I was the victim of a sophisticated imposter scam in which criminals falsely represented themselves as XXXX, our electric utility provider, and fraudulently induced me to send money. On XXXX XXXX XXXX, I received calls from individuals claiming to be representatives of XXXX. They threatened that the electricity to my business would be disconnected immediately if payment was not made that day. As a small business owner, this was an urgent and frightening situation. I had every reason to believe I was speaking with my utility company, and I followed the instructions I was given to make the payment through XXXX. I later learned that these individuals were scammers impersonating XXXX. This was not a legitimate payment to a merchant. It was a payment obtained through fraud, deception, and intimidation. Throughout this dispute, I submitted documentation supporting my claim, including screenshots, dates, and evidence demonstrating that this was a documented XXXX imposter scam. I also filed reports regarding this fraud with the appropriate authorities. Despite this evidence, KeyBanks response fails to address the fraud itself. Instead, KeyBank simply states that the transaction was processed correctly and was therefore appropriately denied. That does not answer the issue I raised. The fact that a transaction was successfully processed does not resolve whether it was induced by fraud. Additionally, KeyBank acknowledges in its response that I was incorrectly advised regarding provisional credit and admits that misinformation was provided by its representatives. This admission raises additional concerns about whether my claim was investigated thoroughly and handled appropriately from the beginning. Therefore, I respectfully request that KeyBank specifically answer the following questions : * Did KeyBank review all of the screenshots, documentation, dates, and evidence I submitted showing that this was a XXXX imposter scam? * What specific investigative steps were taken to evaluate the fraud itself, rather than simply confirming that the payment was processed? * What provisions of KeyBanks policies or applicable regulations were relied upon to deny reimbursement for a documented imposter scam? * Why was the evidence of fraud insufficient to warrant reimbursement? Simply repeating that the dispute was appropriately denied is not an explanation. I am requesting a clear description of how KeyBank evaluated the evidence I provided and why it concluded that the documented fraud did not alter the outcome. I am also requesting that KeyBank refund the full amount of {$1400.00} that was fraudulently obtained through this imposter scam. I acted in good faith under the belief that I was making a legitimate payment to my electric company to prevent my business from being shut off. Instead, I was deceived by criminals. I should not bear the financial loss resulting from this fraud. I respectfully request that the CFPB require KeyBank to conduct a meaningful review of the evidence submitted, provide a substantive explanation for its decision, and reconsider its denial. Based on the facts and documentation provided, I respectfully request that KeyBank reverse its decision and issue a full refund of the {$1400.00} taken through this fraudulent scheme. As a small business owner, I acted under the reasonable belief that I was protecting my business from an immediate utility shutoff. Criminals exploited that belief by impersonating my electric company and using threats to coerce payment. This was not an ordinary authorized purchaseit was a transaction induced through fraud. Thank you for your continued review of this matter. XXXX XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, MA XXXX Phone : ( XXXX ) XXXX Date : XX/XX/year> Subject : Formal Complaint Regarding Unreasonable Account Restriction, Failure to Provide Information, and Denial of Access to My Funds To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this formal complaint regarding the handling of my M & T Bank account and the continued restriction that has prevented me from accessing my own funds for nearly three weeks without any meaningful communication or resolution. On XX/XX/year>, I was unable to access my online banking account. I immediately contacted M & T Bank customer service and was instructed to visit a local branch to verify my identity. On XX/XX/year>, I went to the M & T Bank branch located on XXXX XXXX in XXXX, Massachusetts. While at the branch, I successfully made a deposit of {$270.00}, confirming that my identity had been verified well enough to conduct a transaction. I then met with a bank representative who contacted the individual responsible for placing a legal hold on my account. I was informed that my account had been restricted because there had been multiple attempts to compromise my online banking. I answered every question asked regarding my internet usage, mobile phone, and account activity. I explained that I had not provided my banking information to anyone and was unaware of any unauthorized activity. After remaining at the branch for approximately an hour and a half, I was told that an investigation would be conducted and that someone would contact me with an update. Since then, I have repeatedly attempted to obtain information regarding my account. I contacted M & T Bank on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. Every time I called, I was told that someone would contact me, but no one ever has. I also spoke with representatives in the Retail Department, including XXXX and XXXX, who refused to transfer me to the Fraud Department or allow me to speak with anyone capable of providing answers. I was repeatedly told only that my issue had been escalated and that I would receive a callback. Despite these assurances, I have received no communication whatsoever. As of today, nearly three weeks have passed. My account remains restricted, I have been unable to access or withdraw my own money, and I have received no explanation regarding the status of the investigation, no estimated timeline for resolution, and no written communication explaining why my funds continue to be withheld. This lack of communication and prolonged restriction has caused significant financial hardship and has prevented me from accessing money that belongs to me. Consumers have important rights under both federal law and Massachusetts law. Financial institutions are expected to investigate suspected fraud promptly, communicate with their customers in a timely manner, and provide reasonable access to deposit accounts once identity has been verified. Massachusetts law also requires banks to act in good faith in their dealings with customers, and unfair or deceptive acts or practices may violate Massachusetts General Laws Chapter XXXX, the Massachusetts Consumer Protection Act. Additionally, federal consumer protection laws require financial institutions to maintain fair procedures when restricting customer accounts and to investigate potential fraud within a reasonable period. At this point, I respectfully demand the following : 1. Immediate written confirmation explaining the legal basis for the restriction on my account. 2. A detailed status update regarding the investigation. 3. A specific timeline for when I will regain access to my funds. 4. Immediate restoration of access to my account if there is no lawful basis for continuing the restriction. 5. A written response addressing why I have repeatedly been denied information despite numerous requests over the past three weeks. If this matter is not resolved promptly, I will continue pursuing complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the Massachusetts Division of Banks, and any other appropriate regulatory agencies. I also reserve all legal rights available to me under state and federal law. I expect a prompt written response and immediate attention to this matter. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

After completing the account opening process, I was informed by a Bank of America representative that my business account was active. During a subsequent phone call, I was specifically advised that I did not need to complete any additional consent process because the consent request had been generated using an incorrect phone number that Bank of America entered into its system. Since the phone number on file was inaccurate, I was unable to complete the requested verification. Despite being told that my account was already open and that no further action was required on my part, I continue to receive letters from XXXX XXXX stating that my account has been closed due to my failure to provide consent. These repeated notices directly contradict the information I received from Bank of America 's own representatives and have caused unnecessary confusion and frustration. I respectfully request that Bank of America investigate the following : Why am I continuing to receive letters stating that my account has been closed for failure to provide consent when I was informed that my business account was successfully opened? Why has this issue not been corrected after it was determined that the consent request was generated because Bank of America entered the wrong phone number? Why is XXXX XXXX continuing to send these notices when Bank of America 's representatives have already confirmed that my account is open and active? I request that these inaccurate notices stop immediately unless there is a legitimate issue that requires my attention. I also have a separate concern regarding the initial funding of my account. A Bank of America representative named XXXX obtained my payment information to fund my business account with {$100.00}. I was informed that this amount would be deposited into my new account. However, my account continues to reflect a {$0.00} balance, and I have not received an explanation as to why the initial deposit has not been credited. In addition, I have been experiencing ongoing issues with my account 's email notifications. My correct business email address is on file with Bank of America. However, when I request notifications, statements, or other account communications to be sent to my email, I do not receive them. I have reported this issue to Bank of America representatives, and I was told not to worry because I receive notifications through my phone number. That response is not acceptable. I expect my account to function properly through both communication methods. If my email address is correctly listed on my account, I should receive account notifications, statements, and other communications by email as requested. Simply receiving text messages does not resolve the issue or replace the email functionality that should already be available. I am requesting that Bank of America investigate and resolve the following : Why I continue to receive inaccurate notices stating that my account is closed. Why the incorrect phone number issue was not properly corrected. Why the repeated correspondence from XXXX XXXX continues despite my account being active. Why my {$100.00} initial deposit has not appeared in my account. Why my email notifications and statements are not being delivered even though my correct business email address is on file. What corrective actions Bank of America will take to ensure these issues are permanently resolved. I have previously submitted a complaint regarding related issues. This letter serves as an additional complaint documenting the continued problems I have experienced. I respectfully request a written response explaining the findings of your investigation and the steps Bank of America will take to correct these matters. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

My complaint is that Bank of America has continued to hold the funds indefinitely without providing a clear explanation, a reasonable timeline, or a resolution to its investigation. I understand that Bank of America has the right to investigate a deposit when it believes additional verification is necessary. However, I have contacted the bank numerous times over the past several months seeking information about the status of the investigation. During each call, I have asked why the investigation remains open, whether any additional information is needed from me, whether there is a case number, and whether there is an estimated completion date. No one has been able to explain what remains under investigation or what is preventing the investigation from being completed. Additionally, I have repeatedly requested that, if Bank of America is unable or unwilling to release the funds, the check and any associated funds be promptly returned to the Internal Revenue Service rather than being held indefinitely. Despite these repeated requests, Bank of America has neither returned the funds to the IRS nor provided any explanation as to why they continue to retain them. I am not asking the CFPB to determine ownership of the check. Rather, I am requesting that Bank of America provide a clear written explanation of why the investigation remains open, identify the legal and factual basis for continuing to hold the funds, explain why the funds have not been returned to the IRS despite my repeated requests, provide a reasonable timeline for resolving this matter, and take the appropriate action to either release the funds if legally permissible or promptly return them to the Internal Revenue Service if they can not be released. In addition, I have repeatedly requested that, if Bank of America is unable or unwilling to release the funds, the check and the associated funds be promptly returned to the Internal Revenue Service ( IRS ) rather than being held indefinitely. Despite these repeated requests, the bank has neither returned the funds to the IRS nor explained why they continue to retain them. At this point, I am simply seeking transparency, a timely resolution, and a written explanation of Bank of Americas actions.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding PNC Banks denial of approximately {$12000.00} in unauthorized transactions on my deposit account. I want to begin by emphasizing that I have been a very happy and loyal PNC customer. I appreciate PNC and have generally been pleased with the services I have received. I sincerely hope to continue my relationship with the bank. I am not submitting this complaint to attack PNC or its employees. I am respectfully asking for reconsideration, compassion, and a complete review of an extremely serious situation that has caused me severe financial hardship. I reported more than XXXX unauthorized transactions that occurred beginning approximately XX/XX/year>. The transactions consisted primarily of XXXX and XXXX purchases, along with one or more rent-related payments. I did not make, authorize, approve, or benefit from the transactions I reported. PNC initially issued provisional credit for certain transactions, which I sincerely appreciate. However, PNCs retail investigations team subsequently denied most of the older disputed transactions, totaling approximately {$12000.00}. I was informed that the primary reason for the denial was that the transactions were reported outside the applicable reporting period. I understand that financial institutions have reporting deadlines and must follow established investigation procedures. However, I respectfully believe that applying the deadline without fully considering my extraordinary circumstances produces a deeply unfair result. During the period in question, I was in XXXX and had no meaningful or reliable access to the internet, online banking, account statements, alerts, or other information that would have allowed me to discover and report the transactions sooner. I did not knowingly ignore the transactions, neglect my account, or intentionally wait to report them. I was genuinely unaware that the activity was occurring and lacked the practical ability to monitor my account. As soon as I became aware of the unauthorized activity and was able to address it, I contacted PNC and reported the transactions. The delay was not voluntary and was not caused by indifference. It resulted from circumstances outside my control. I respectfully ask PNC and the CFPB to consider the provisions of the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E, including 12 C.F.R. 1005.6. Regulation E generally requires consumers to report unauthorized electronic fund transfers within established periods, but it also recognizes that those periods should be extended to a reasonable time when extenuating circumstances, such as extended travel or hospitalization, prevent timely notification. My extended presence overseas, my location in XXXX, and my lack of meaningful internet and account access are directly relevant to why I could not provide earlier notice. I respectfully request that PNC evaluate those circumstances rather than treating the normal reporting period as an absolute bar without exception. I am not asking PNC to approve my claim without investigation. I am asking PNC to reopen the denied portion of my claim, examine the evidence, and determine whether the transactions were actually authorized by me. I respectfully request that PNC review available evidence including : 1. The delivery addresses associated with the XXXX and XXXX orders. 2. The names, email addresses, telephone numbers, devices, and accounts used to place the orders. 3. IP addresses and device-location information associated with the purchases. 4. My PNC online-banking login and device history during the relevant period. 5. The recipient and account information connected to the rent-related payments. 6. The geographic difference between my documented location and the locations where the purchases, deliveries, or payments occurred. 7. Consumer complaint narrative: My name is XXXX XXXX, and I am submitting this formal complaint regarding my recent experience with the World Finance branch located at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, Missouri XXXX. I am requesting that World Finance Corporate, Compliance, and Ethics departments conduct a complete review and investigation into the handling of my personal loan application, the communication surrounding the application process, and the failure to provide me with timely and adequate information regarding the decision made on my application. On or around XX/XX/year>, I submitted an application for a personal loan in the amount of {$12000.00} through the World Finance branch located at the address listed above. I applied in good faith and provided the requested information necessary for the company to evaluate my application, including information relating to my employment, income, identity, and intended use of the requested loan proceeds. I entered into this process expecting a professional and transparent lending experience. I understand that lenders have underwriting requirements and that not every application is approved. However, regardless of the final lending decision, consumers deserve to be treated fairly, communicated with professionally, and provided with appropriate explanations when adverse decisions are made. My concern is not simply that my application was denied. My concern is the manner in which my application was handled, the lack of follow-up communication, the failure to provide the promised callback, and the absence of a clear written explanation regarding the reasons for the denial. Background Regarding My Loan Application After submitting my application, I was contacted by a World Finance representative named XXXX XXXX. During our conversation, XXXX XXXX asked me questions regarding my loan request, including questions about why I wanted the funds and what I intended to use the money for. I explained that the requested funds were for legitimate personal expenses, including repairs and maintenance related to my XXXX XXXX. Specifically, I explained that the funds were needed for necessary vehicle-related expenses, including : New tires ; Brake repairs ; Vehicle sensor repairs ; and Other maintenance-related expenses. I also provided information regarding my employment and income. I explained that I earn approximately {$5700.00} every two weeks. I answered the questions presented to me and fully cooperated throughout the process. I understand that lenders may ask questions regarding loan purpose, income, employment, and financial circumstances as part of their underwriting process. However, during the conversation, I felt that the discussion became unnecessarily focused on questioning my personal financial decisions rather than evaluating my application based on my qualifications and the information provided. I was willing to provide information necessary for the application review process, but I expected the interaction to remain professional, respectful, and focused on the actual lending criteria. Promised Callback That Never Occurred At the conclusion of my conversation with XXXX XXXX, I was specifically advised that he would call me back within approximately one hour regarding the status of my application. Based on that statement, I reasonably expected a follow-up communication regarding whether additional documentation was needed, whether my application required further review, or whether a decision had been made. However, that callback never occurred. I did not receive the promised phone call. I was not contacted by XXXX XXXX to explain the status of my application. I was not informed directly that my application had been denied. Instead, I later learned that my application had been denied without receiving the communication that had been promised to me. This lack of communication was concerning because I had taken the time to provide information, answer questions, and cooperate with the application process. At a minimum, I believe I should have received a professional follow-up explaining the outcome. Failure to Receive Written Explanation of Denial After learning that my loan application was denied, I expected to receive a written explanation identifying the reasons for the decision. As of the date of this complaint, I have not received a written adverse action notice explaining the principal reasons for the denial of my application. A consumer should not be left guessing why a financial decision was made, particularly when that decision affects access to credit. A written explanation is important because it allows consumers to : Understand the basis of the decision ; Correct possible errors ; Address issues affecting future applications ; Determine whether inaccurate information was used ; Exercise applicable consumer rights. Without a written explanation, I have no way of knowing whether the decision was based on : Credit information ; Verification issues ; Income considerations ; Documentation concerns ; Underwriting criteria ; Internal policies ; or Any other factor. I respectfully request that World Finance provide the complete adverse action notice associated with my application, including the principal reasons for the denial. Concerns Regarding Application Handling My concerns regarding this matter include, but are not limited to, the following : 1. Failure to provide promised follow-up communication I was specifically told that I would receive a callback within one hour. That communication never occurred. Consumers should not be told they will receive follow-up communication and then receive no response. 2. Lack of transparency regarding the denial decision I was denied but was not provided with a clear explanation of why the application was declined. A transparent lending process requires that consumers understand the basis for significant financial decisions. 3. Lack of professionalism during the application review While I understand that lenders may ask questions about loan purpose and financial circumstances, I felt the conversation became unnecessarily focused on challenging my personal reasons for requesting the loan rather than objectively reviewing my application. 4. An account she has been actively managing with me for several years, yet the account does not show up on her credit reports. Wells Fargo has acknowledged that they furnish authorized user information to the credit bureaus but advised they do not collect Social Security numbers for authorized users on my account. I believe the absence of sufficient identifying information is the sole reason preventing the account from being matched to her credit file because it is not showing up. If Wells Fargo is not providing sufficient identifying information for the bureaus to confidently match the authorized user account to my daughter 's credit file, then the credit bureaus have no information to correct. This is not a dispute over inaccurate payment history, an incorrect balance, or ownership of the account. The resolution I am requesting is for Wells Fargo to provide a process to add my daughter 's Social Security number to her existing authorized user profile and to furnish the updated identifying information to the credit reporting agencies. Directing me to dispute the matter with the credit bureaus does not address the source of the problem, which is the information being furnished by Wells Fargo.

I respectfully request a complete written explanation of the denial, clarification regarding an unexpected balloon payment, and a review of whether the handling of my application adversely affected my credit profile. At this time, I remain unclear about the specific reasons my refinance application was denied. During conversations with the lender, I was told that the denial involved references to " investors '' and the absence of a Form XXXX. However, these explanations were vague and insufficient, and I still do not understand how these factors affected my eligibility or resulted in the denial of my application. What is particularly concerning is that my refinance was denied only after I had completed and signed all the closing documents. I attended the scheduled closing, executed all required paperwork, and provided my XXXX XXXX with the required check for the transfer of funds. Based on the lender 's actions and the completion of the closing process, I reasonably believed the refinance had been approved and was moving forward. The subsequent denial, after all closing documents had been executed, was unexpected and has never been adequately explained. Throughout the refinance process, I acted honestly and in good faith. I fully disclosed my updated salary structure and the way I am compensated. Although my method of compensation changed, my employer, position, and employment status did not. In fact, my income has increased significantly, and I have remained continuously employed in the same position for more than XXXX and a half years. I could have chosen not to disclose the change in my compensation structure, but I believed it was important to be completely transparent and truthful throughout the underwriting process. From the beginning of the application, I fully cooperated with every documentation request. On XX/XX/XXXX, I promptly submitted the requested pay stubs. Because the underwriting process extended for approximately XXXX months, I was later asked to provide additional documentation, which I supplied without delay. This included : An employer verification letter ; Evidence of consistent direct deposits ; Documentation demonstrating stable and ongoing income ; A written explanation of my salary structure ; and Any additional information requested to verify my continued employment and ability to repay the loan. Despite providing every document requested, my application was ultimately denied without a meaningful explanation of how my documentation was evaluated or why it was considered insufficient. My employment remained stable throughout the entire review period. I have been a PHH Mortgage customer for more than XXXX years and have maintained a longstanding relationship with the company. Given my payment history, stable employment, increased income, and full cooperation throughout the refinance process, I expected my complete financial profile to be fairly and thoroughly evaluated. During the refinance process, I was also informed for the first time that my mortgage may include an approximately {$80000.00} balloon payment due at maturity. This information came as a complete surprise and was the primary reason I sought to refinance my loan. I have never received a clear explanation or documentation supporting this obligation. Accordingly, I request complete documentation identifying : The contractual basis for the balloon payment ; The exact amount due ; The date it becomes payable ; The loan documents establishing this obligation ; and Any available options to satisfy, refinance, or otherwise avoid the balloon payment. This information is essential so that I can properly understand my future financial obligations and make informed financial decisions. I am also deeply concerned about the effect this refinance application may have had on my credit profile. Because the refinance was denied after an extended review period, I am now required to seek alternative financing much sooner than expected. Since the credit inquiry associated with this refinance application, I have experienced unexpected denials for other forms of credit. Specifically, I was denied financing for necessary dental treatment despite having been approved for similar financing only XXXX years ago when my credit profile was significantly weaker than it is today. I was also denied while attempting to open a business bank account. While I recognize that lending decisions are based on multiple factors, the refinance application and related credit inquiry appear to be the only significant changes to my credit profile during this period. As a result, I am concerned that the handling or reporting of this application may have adversely affected my ability to obtain credit. This experience has caused me significant financial XXXX XXXX XXXX. I entered the refinance process in good faith, believing it would improve my financial situation and provide certainty regarding my mortgage. Instead, after months of providing documentation, complying with every request, completing the closing process, and believing my loan had been approved, I was left with an unexplained denial, uncertainty surrounding a substantial balloon payment, and unexpected difficulty obtaining other forms of credit. My mortgage is scheduled to mature in XXXX. The uncertainty surrounding the reported balloon payment and the denial of my refinance have left me with serious concerns about my future financial obligations and my ability to obtain financing before my loan matures. I can't seek other financing options. I appreciate the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau 's attention to this matter and respectfully request a thorough investigation and assistance in obtaining the information necessary to understand the lender 's actions and to determine whether the refinance process was handled fairly and in accordance with applicable consumer protection laws. Sincerely, XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative: I obtained an installment loan through Affirm on XX/XX/year>, during the purchase of a custom XXXX portrait. My dispute is not about the merchant 's refund policy. It concerns the circumstances under which the financing was obtained and Affirm 's handling of my dispute. I explained to Affirm that I believe I was induced to enter into the financed transaction through deceptive and unconscionable sales practices. Before my appointment, including during a required XXXX preparation call, I was never informed that I would be expected to make a same-day purchasing decision involving portrait packages costing thousands of dollars. Pricing was first disclosed only after the portrait session. During the sales presentation, I was encouraged to finance the purchase through Affirm. The merchant did not verbally disclose that the order would be non-cancelable or provide a meaningful opportunity for me to review those terms before I signed the agreement. After the financing was completed, the salesperson held the paperwork, pointed to signature lines, and directed me where to sign. I was not given a meaningful opportunity to read the agreement before signing and did not become aware of the non-cancellation language until I reviewed the documents after returning home. When I contacted Affirm, I explained that my dispute concerned the sales practices used to obtain the financed transaction. Because none of Affirm 's dispute categories fit my situation, I was instructed to submit the dispute through the return/cancellation process even though no completed portrait had been delivered and there was nothing to return. I believe this caused my dispute to be evaluated solely under the merchant 's refund policy rather than the deceptive sales practices I reported. I submitted supporting documentation, but Affirm denied my dispute solely because the merchant stated it followed its refund policy. The decision did not address the specific allegations or evidence I submitted regarding the sales practices that induced the financed transaction .. Affirm did not address my allegations that the cancellation policy was not disclosed before the transaction, that I was not given a meaningful opportunity to review the agreement before signing, or the deceptive and unconscionable sales practices that formed the basis of my dispute. The Kansas Attorney General 's XXXX XXXX XXXX has opened an active investigation into the merchant 's sales practices. I informed Affirm of the pending investigation. After the denial, an Affirm representative advised me to appeal, but no appeal option or appeal process was available. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate whether Affirm conducted a reasonable and good-faith investigation of my dispute and whether its dispute process fairly addresses disputes involving alleged deceptive and unconscionable sales practices that induce consumers to enter into financed transactions.

Consumer complaint narrative: In XX/XX/XXXX I financed a pool cleaner from XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX using a 12-month installment loan from Affirm. The loan was originated XX/XX/XXXX for {$820.00} at 11.01 % APR. The order was cancelled. It never shipped. I never received the merchandise. On XX/XX/XXXX XXXX days after the loan was originated XXXX XXXX XXXXefunded the full {$820.00} back to Affirm. I have XXXX 's internal refund record, which states : Status REFUNDED; Returned, Resolved, and Disbursed XX/XX/XXXX ; Total Refunded {$820.00} ; Method of Payment : Affirm ; Check/Document Number XXXX. XXXXXXXX XXXX order record shows the order status as " XXXX Cancelled '' and states " REFUND COMPLETED '' and " XXXX Has Refunded. '' Affirm never applied that refund to my loan. Affirm never notified me the refund had been received. Affirm continued to bill me. I paid the loan in full, with interest, and paid it off on XX/XX/XXXX. Affirm 's own debt validation letter dated XX/XX/XXXX confirms the loan as " Paid in Full. '' Affirm was therefore paid twice for one {$820.00} transaction once by the merchant on XX/XX/XXXX, and once by me over the followin g twelve months, with interest for goods I never received. I did not notice the improper charge at the time because I had made two nearly identical purchases from the same merchant in the same period. After XXXX 's cancelled the first pool cleaner order ( the item was back-ordered ), I ordered a different brand of pool cleaner from the same merchant at a similar price, also financed through Affirm. I received that second one. Because I had two Affirm loans of similar amounts to the same merchant in the same window, the payments on the cancelled order did not stand out to me as duplicative. I discovered the problem in XX/XX/XXXX, when I reviewed my records in my Affirm account and realized I had paid Affirm for two pool cleaners but received only one. I then asked XXXXXXXXXXXX XXXX to research the cancelled order. XXXXXXXX XXXX retrieved its records and produced the refund documentation showing it had returned the full {$820.00} to Affirm on XX/XX/XXXX. Until XXXXXXXX XXXX produced those records, I had no way to know a refund had ever been made. Only Affirm had visibility into what the merchant remitted to Affirm, and Affirm never told me. Critically, Affirm has now confirmed the refund date itself. In a live chat on XX/XX/XXXX, an Affirm supervisor reviewing my account wrote to me : " The refund was processed on XX/XX/XXXX and your last payment on loan was on XX/XX/XXXX. '' That matches the merchant 's records exactly. In the same chat, the same supervisor quoted me Affirm 's own policy : " If the merchant completes processing a full refund ... Any payments already made will be refunded to your original form of payment, less any accrued interest, within 3-10 business days. '' Affirm stated its own obligation and then refused to perform it. Affirm 's sole basis for refusing is an internal policy that a dispute can not be opened more than 120 days after the purchase. That policy is not responsive. A 120-day window governs how long Affirm will pursue a merchant for a refund. It can not govern Affirm 's obligation to remit a refund the merchant already sent to Affirm. Affirm does not acquire ownership of my money because an internal deadline expired particularly when the only reason I missed that deadline is that Affirm never disclosed that the money had come back. On XX/XX/XXXX I spent over three hours in Affirm 's chat. I was passed through five agents and transferred to a " supervisor '' three separate times. After nearly two hours the chat dropped and I was returned to the general queue to start over. One agent escalated my case and promised a response in 3-5 business days, then transferred me away and the escalation disappeared this has happened repeatedly for months. An agent instructed me to email my evidence to Affirm 's customer care address ; that address auto-replied telling me to open a new case. A new case I am prevented from opening, because it is outside of their 120 day policy window. I asked at least six times for one document : proof that Affirm disbursed funds to XXXXXXXX XXXX and an accounting of what happened to the {$820.00} XXXXXXXX XXXX returned. No agent produced it. I was told the loan date and loan amount were " the only information we can provide. '' I also asked for a transcript of my own dispute conversation and was told Affirm is " not able '' to send one. I copied the transcript and pasted it into my own notes. Requested resolution : Refund of the full amount I paid on this loan {$870.00} in principal and interest plus interest on that sum from XX/XX/XXXX, the date Affirm received the merchant 's refund. A written accounting of the disposition of the {$820.00} XXXXXXXX XXXX disbursed to Affirm on XX/XX/XXXX, referenced by XXXXXXXX XXXX check/document number XXXX. I also ask the Bureau to consider whether this is systemic. If Affirm 's systems do not reliably credit consumers when merchants return funds on cancelled orders, and the 120-day policy is then used to refuse consumers who find out late, then every Affirm borrower whose order was cancelled and refunded is exposed to paying for goods they never received while Affirm keeps the merchant 's money. I would never have known had I not audited my own account four years later and then asked the merchant to retrieve records from XXXX.

Between XX/XX/year>, and XX/XX/year>, I contacted American Express and XXXX numerous times to inquire about the status of my refund. During these communications, I received inconsistent and conflicting information. On some occasions, representatives stated that they could not locate my previously submitted documentation. On other occasions, I was advised that the refund check had already been mailed and that I simply needed to continue waiting. Despite repeated follow-up efforts, I did not receive the promised refund. On XX/XX/year>, after waiting more than four months without receiving the refund, I sent an email to American Express requesting immediate resolution and advising that I would file a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) if the matter was not resolved. Product: Checking or savings account
Sub-issue: Funds not handled or disbursed as instructed
Consumer complaint narrative: My monthly VA disability compensation and my OPM disability retirement benefits were directly deposited into my USAA Federal Savings Bank checking account. Both are federal benefit payments protected under 38 U.S.C. 5301 ( a ) ( VA ) and 5 U.S.C. 8346 and 8470 ( OPM ), and are recognized as protected federal benefits under 31 CFR Part 212. My USAA account currently shows a negative balance. That negative balance exists only because USAA credited my account with funds that were fraudulently taken and then clawed those funds back. Those charges are still actively being disputed as fraudulent and have not been resolved. USAA is applying my protected federal disability and retirement funds against this disputed negative balance. On or about XX/XX/year>, I called USAA and spoke with a member of the Member Relations Team ( MRT ), who confirmed that these funds were federally protected benefits, that they should not be applied to the negative balance, and that they would be rejected and sent back to the U.S. Treasury rather than applied to the balance. That call was recorded by USAA. USAA can locate and review the recorded call from on or about XX/XX/year>, in which its representative confirmed the funds were protected and would be rejected and returned to the U.S. Treasury. This confirmation was also entered into my account annotations/notes. On XX/XX/year>, at approximately XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX, I spoke with another USAA MRT representative, named XXXX. I explained repeatedly that the funds were to have been rejected, that my account is negative only because USAA credited it with the fraudulently taken funds and then clawed them back, and that the representative I spoke with on XX/XX/year>, told me the funds were federally protected benefits that should not be applied to the negative balance and should instead be sent back to the U.S. Treasury. This call was also recorded, and USAA advised me it would be recorded. USAA can reference the recorded call from XX/XX/year>, at approximately XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX During that call, the representative reviewed the documents on USAAs end and confirmed that the funds were in fact processed to be sent back and that USAAs records show they should have been returned. She stated USAA sent these documents on XX/XX/year>, and that the process typically takes 7 to 10 business days. That 7-to-10 business day window has now fully elapsed, and USAA has still not completed the return of my protected funds. This process is taking entirely too long, and I remain without access to one of my only sources of income. I am homeless and completely without money to buy food. I am going hungry. Later in that same call, the representative told me to reach out to the VA and OPM regarding the funds. This directly contradicts what she had just confirmed that USAA itself processed the return on XX/XX/year>, and that the funds were on USAAs end awaiting completion within USAAs own 7-to-10 business day timeframe. Following her instruction, I contacted the VA, and the VA was unable to locate my VA disability funds and confirmed the money has not been sent back to them. This confirms that USAA has not actually completed the return it claims to have processed. The funds are not in the possession of the VA or OPM, and it is USAA not the VA or OPM that initiated and controls the pending return. Redirecting me to the VA and OPM is an improper attempt to shift responsibility for completing a process that USAA already started and that its own records show should have been finished. Separately, and I believe as a direct result of a prior CFPB complaint I filed against USAA, USAA has elected to no longer do business with me and is closing my accounts. USAA has given no reason for this action other than the fact that I exercised my right to file a complaint. I believe this is retaliation against me for filing a CFPB complaint. USAAs own recorded calls, account annotations, and internal documents confirm its representatives have repeatedly acknowledged these are protected federal benefits that should have been rejected and returned to the U.S. Treasury. Despite these acknowledgments and USAAs own records showing the funds were processed to be sent back on XX/XX/year>, USAA has failed to complete the process within its own stated 7-to-10 business day timeframe, and the receiving agency confirms the funds have not arrived. I am asking the CFPB to require USAA to immediately complete the return of my protected VA and OPM benefit funds to the U.S. Treasury. Desired resolution : Immediate completion of the rejection and return of my VA disability and OPM disability retirement funds to the U.S. Treasury ; a written explanation of why the return was not completed within USAAs own stated 7-to-10 business day timeframe after being processed on XX/XX/year>, when the receiving agency confirms it has not received the funds ; cessation of applying protected federal benefits to a disputed, unresolved account balance ; resolution of the pending fraud dispute ; confirmation that USAA not the VA or OPM is responsible for completing the return it processed on XX/XX/year> ; and an explanation of USAAs decision to close my accounts following my prior complaint.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint to report a pattern of predatory and discriminatory lending, deceptive practices, and abusive servicing by Exeter Finance LLC and its originating dealer, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, MO ), in connection with the financing of my XXXX XXXX Yukon.In XX/XX/XXXX, I attempted to purchase the vehicle. This was presented not as an option but as a non-negotiable requirement from the lender, Exeter Finance. This constitutes a deceptive and unfair practice under the Missouri Merchandising Practices Act, as it was a material misrepresentation designed to extract the maximum possible cash from me at origination. The dealer also refused to negotiate on the vehicle price, stating the sticker price was as low as they could go.During negotiations, the dealer stated that to be approved, I would need either the substantial down payment or a co-signer with a strong credit history and income equal to my own. This constitutes an adverse action under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), 15 U.S.C. 1691. I was never provided with the mandatory written adverse action notice explaining why a co-signer was required, a direct violation of federal law.On multiple occasions, I have requested short-term extensions of a week or XXXX to bring my account current. Instead of granting a simple extension, Exeter XXXX stated that the only way they could help was to place the delinquent payments on the back of the loan. I never requested this modification. This unilateral capitalization of delinquent payments is an unauthorized modification of the contract, designed to extend the loan term and maximize interest charges. This violates both the Missouri Motor Vehicle Time Sales Law ( RSMo 365.130 ) and the Illinois Motor Vehicle Retail Installment Sales Act ( 815 ILCS 375/19 ), which require such extensions to be made only upon the buyers explicit request.Exeter has reported late payments to credit reporting agencies for the same periods in which it unilaterally deferred payments through back-ending. A creditor can not simultaneously modify a loan to defer a payment and report that same payment as delinquent to credit bureaus. This constitutes furnishing inaccurate information in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ). This inaccurate reporting has caused significant damage to my credit profile.I am a XXXX XXXX XXXX. Exeter 's and its dealer 's conduct must be viewed through the lens of federal and state fair lending and civil rights laws. Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ), 15 U.S.C. 1691, race and sex are prohibited bases for any form of credit discrimination. Under the Civil Rights Act of 1866, 42 U.S.C. 1981, all persons have the same right to make and enforce contracts as is enjoyed by white citizens, which includes " the enjoyment of all benefits, privileges, terms, and conditions of the contractual relationship. '' Under the Illinois XXXXuman Rights Act, 775 ILCS 5/4-102, it is a state civil rights violation for any financial institution to deny or vary the terms of a loan on the basis of race or sex. The standardized " cosigner or cash '' script, when applied to a XXXX XXXX borrower, constitutes potential disparate treatment and disparate impact discrimination. The CFPB and Department of Justice have investigated and entered into substantial monetary settlements with auto lenders for charging borrowers XXXX XXXX higher costs and imposing discriminatory terms. Exeters requirement that I produce a co-signer with " strong credit and equal income '' or a " substantial down payment, '' while potentially offering different and less onerous terms to similarly situated non-Black applicants, constitutes unlawful discrimination in the terms and conditions of my contract. Furthermore, the predatory servicing practices ( unauthorized back-ending, refusal to refinance, continued collection harassment ) when applied to a XXXX borrower constitute post-formation discrimination in the performance and modification of the contract, a direct violation of 42 U.S.C. 1981 ( b ).

Once an account reflects a XXXX balance because it has been written off, sold, transferred, or otherwise resolved, the information reported must accurately reflect the account 's true status. Reporting information that is incomplete, misleading, or inaccurate may violate the FCRA. I respectfully request that the CFPB require Exeter Finance LLC and the consumer reporting agencies to : Conduct a complete investigation into this account. Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing a formal consumer complaint against Caine & Weiner Company , Inc. for direct non-compliance with the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g, and CFPB Regulation F ( 12 CFR 1006.34 ) governing debt validation requirements. On XX/XX/year>, I submitted a formal written Debt Validation Request explicitly demanding three specific categories of records : ( 1 ) A complete transaction history and itemized accounting explaining the calculation of the alleged {$550.00} balance ; ( 2 ) Documentation supporting the underlying consumer obligation with the original creditor ; and ( 3 ) Documentation establishing Caine & Weiners legal authority to collect and furnish information concerning this specific account. Under CFPB Regulation F ( 12 CFR 1006.34 ), a debt collector must provide a consumer with clear, itemized data if requested. Caine & Weiners mailed response completely failed to meet these mandates. They provided only a generic cover letter and a single-page XXXX final bill summary. Crucially, Caine & Weiners own correspondence explicitly admits that the balance differences are the result of adjustments made to the account by the creditor. Despite making this representation, the company completely failed to include any transaction history, payment ledger, or underlying records identifying those adjustments or explaining how they affected the balance now being asserted. A summary final billing statement that merely lists a total amount completely fails to satisfy verification obligations under 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) when a consumer has explicitly disputed the underlying calculations and accounting entries. Furthermore, demanding a balance that relies on un-itemized, hidden 'adjustments ' constitutes a direct violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ) for misrepresenting the true legal character, nature, and amount of an alleged consumer debt. To further demonstrate their total lack of data integrity, the XXXX billing statement relies on an incorrect historical address ( XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, PA ) that completely contradicts my current verified address. I appealed that determination and submitted payment records from the prior servicer, together with bank statements showing that the trial payments had been made. While the payment dispute was being investigated, I was unable to continue making my regular mortgage payments because the trial modification had already been marked as unsuccessful. After the review, I was informed that I could continue if I paid XXXX months of mortgage payments within XXXX days. Unfortunately, I did not receive that notice until approximately XXXX and a half weeks after it had been mailed, making it impossible to respond within the required timeframe, even though I had the funds available to make those payments. I was later informed that an email had been sent to my personal email account on file and that they attempted to reach me by phone. I never received the email and respectfully believe that such an important, time-sensitive notice should have been communicated through the secure mortgage portal and by mail with sufficient time to respond. I later entered a second trial loan modification with a required trial payment of {$5400.00}. During that trial, I experienced a financial hardship and was unable to complete XXXX scheduled payment. I immediately contacted the servicer to explain my circumstances. Although that trial modification was unsuccessful, I remained committed to keeping my home and continued working with my mortgage servicers to pursue every available home-retention option. During my third trial loan modification, my required trial payment was {$5300.00}. I successfully made XXXX of the required trial payments and was attempting to make the final trial payment on XX/XX/scrub>XXXX XXXX XXXX On this date, I repeatedly attempted to make a payment by telephone. Unfortunately, I could only submit payments with a customer service representative over the phone. I called multiple times and was on hold for over an hour due to unusually high call volumes. I spent several hours on hold due to unusually high call volume and was unable to reach a representative before customer service closed, and my call was disconnected. As a result, my payment could not be processed, and the trial modification was denied. During this time, my loan was transferred to Champion Mortgage. Following that denial, I submitted a new application for mortgage assistance. On XX/XX/year>, I received a Mortgage Assistance Determination Letter advising that I could appeal the modification decision within XXXX calendar days. I mailed my appeal by certified mail on XX/XX/year>XXXX within the required timeframe. The letter stated that I would receive a written appeal decision within XXXX calendar days after the servicer received my appeal. After submitting my appeal, I contacted Champion Mortgage several times to confirm that it had been received. During one conversation, I was informed by a representative that the company did not have to consider my appeal and that the appeal language was simply required to be included in the correspondence. I later received another Mortgage Assistance Determination Letter dated XX/XX/scrub>XXXX XXXX from Champion Mortgage, which appeared substantially similar to the XX/XX/XXXX determination and did not clearly indicate whether it represented the decision on my appeal. As a result, I remain uncertain whether my loss mitigation review was completed on XX/XX/year>, and/or whether my appeal was independently reviewed. I also respectfully request that the servicer provide a complete explanation of its decisions and review whether all applicable loss mitigation procedures were properly followed before proceeding with foreclosure. Throughout my loan modification efforts, I experienced repeated communication issues that I believe affected my ability to complete the loss mitigation process. These issues included delayed or unclear notifications, difficulty obtaining timely information about the status of my modification and appeal, and being unable to reach customer service when a time-sensitive payment was due.
