Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint against Goldman Sachs Bank USA regarding its handling of a billing dispute on my Apple Card. The bank resolved the dispute in the merchant 's favor despite merchant evidence containing a written admission that the contract term used to calculate its invoice was never authorized, and despite documentation that the charge itself was processed without my authorization during an active dispute, in an amount with no valid basis under any contract I signed. I signed one contract with XXXX XXXX XXXX, dated XX/XX/XXXX : a XXXX residential term at {$64.00} per month, totaling {$2300.00} ( Docusign Envelope ID XXXX ). Thirty-six months from XX/XX/XXXX, ends in XX/XX/XXXX, and XXXX itself confirmed this in writing in its response to Better Business Bureau XXXX XXXX : " the previous contract term began on XX/XX/XXXX and was set to end on XX/XX/XXXX. '' I paid faithfully and on time every month from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, as XXXX 's own account history shows. On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX charged me {$69.00}, above my contracted rate of {$64.00}. On XX/XX/XXXX, I called XXXX to ask why my rate had increased, told them I could not afford the higher amount, and asked about cancelling. I was quoted approximately {$940.00} to cancel. On that same call, I asked XXXX to send me a copy of my contract the first copy I had in hand because I wanted to read its terms and was prepared to settle the quoted cancellation amount properly. Rather than accept my cancellation, XXXX retained me with an offer of a reduced rate of {$61.00} per month, which I was told I qualified for as a diligent long-term customer. I paid {$61.00} on XX/XX/XXXX. Because it made no sense that XXXX would raise my rate and then lower it below my original contract rate, I called XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX, to ask why and only then was I told that accepting the reduced rate had added a new XXXX term to my account, extending my contract to XX/XX/XXXX. In its formal BBB response dated XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX admitted this in writing : " a rate reduction was applied to the account that resulted in a new XXXX term being added to the account. The customer confirmed that she did not know the term was extended and did not agree to it. '' When I objected to the extension, XXXX offered to restore the XXXX end date while keeping the {$61.00} rate. I declined, because XXXX had raised my contracted rate once and modified my contract term once, both without disclosure, and I had no confidence the cycle would not repeat. I cancelled, with XXXX setting the effective date at XX/XX/XXXX, per its XXXX notice policy a period already covered by my XX/XX/XXXX payment. On the cancellation call, an XXXX XXXX quoted {$840.00} as the fee under my original XXXX contract. XXXX then instead billed me {$1600.00}, including a Contract Cancellation Charge of {$1600.00} ( Invoice XXXX, dated XX/XX/XXXX ) which, as XXXX 's own invoice and billing statement show, was calculated against a service period of XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX with every line item reflecting XXXX remaining months under the very term XXXX admitted I never authorized. On XX/XX/XXXX, through the BBB, I made a conditional settlement offer solely to end the relationship : I would pay {$840.00} only upon written confirmation that it constituted full and final settlement with a permanent zero balance, no further charges, no collection activity, and no negative credit reporting, and only through an approved installment arrangement, because I stated explicitly that I could not pay a lump sum. Instead, on XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX charged my Apple Card the full {$840.00} in a single transaction. My XX/XX/XXXX, BBB response contemporaneously documents that the payment was processed without my authorization during the active dispute. A conditional offer to settle a disputed amount, on conditions never met, is not authorization and is not an admission that the amount was owed. Upon reflection after the charge posted, I recognized that XXXX had taken {$840.00} from my card with no legal or contractual validity an amount derived from a contract term XXXX itself admitted I never agreed to, processed without my authorization and against my documented written conditions. I therefore raised a dispute with Apple Card XXXX Goldman Sachs ), dispute number XXXX. Goldman Sachs resolved that dispute in the merchant 's favor under reason code XXXX ( representment sequence XXXX, issuer control number XXXX ). At my request, Goldman Sachs provided the merchant 's XXXX representment packet, and my review of that evidence is the basis of this complaint, because the merchant 's own documents disprove the charge. The {$840.00} amount itself has no valid basis under any account XXXX has given of it. On the cancellation call, XXXX represented that {$840.00} was calculated from my original XXXX contract. In writing, however in both its BBB response and its rebuttal letter to Goldman Sachs, which states " payment received is associated with early cancellation charge of {$840.00} out of {$1600.00} was adjusted '' XXXX characterizes the {$840.00} as a discount from the {$1600.00} charge ... a discount derived from an unauthorized charge is itself unauthorized. XXXX 's own account history confirms this arithmetically : it shows the {$1600.00} acceleration billing posted on XX/XX/XXXX, followed by a " Write Off Settlement - XXXX '' of {$760.00} on XX/XX/XXXX, leaving exactly {$840.00} proving the {$840.00} is simply the unwritten-off remainder of the invoice calculated on the unauthorized XXXX term, not an amount computed under my signed contract, and that this figure was fixed internally a week before my XX/XX/XXXX conditional offer. XXXX 's two explanations are also mutually incompatible, and each fails on its own terms : if {$840.00} were truly calculated from the signed XXXX contract, it would approximate that contract 's Paragraph XXXX formula of XXXX XXXX of remaining monthly charges, which from the XX/XX/XXXX cancellation to XX/XX/XXXX, yields approximately {$780.00} at the {$64.00} rate and approximately {$730.00} at the {$61.00} rate not {$840.00}. Under either of XXXX 's own characterizations, no valid {$840.00} obligation existed. I dispute this charge because it was processed without authorization during an active dispute, following an admittedly unauthorized contract modification, in an amount unsupported by any contract. Goldman Sachs was provided my signed contract and the BBB complaint file during the dispute and nonetheless resolved it in the merchant 's favor under reason code XXXX ( representment sequence XXXX, issuer control number XXXX ). I am asking Goldman Sachs to reopen the dispute and reverse the {$840.00} charge in full

Consumer complaint narrative: To whom it may concern, I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau investigate the servicing of my VA home loan due to significant accounting discrepancies that have been identified during my review of the loan records currently available to me. My mortgage loan originated in XX/XX/year> with an original principal balance of approximately {$520000.00}. I began making regular monthly payments in XX/XX/year>. During the XXXX pandemic, I entered into a temporary forbearance program offered under the CARES Act. After the forbearance period, I discovered that the outstanding principal balance of my mortgage had increased dramatically. Based on the documents currently in my possession, the balance increased by approximately {$100000.00} despite only one year of deferred payments. This increase appears disproportionate to the amount that should have been affected by the forbearance and raises substantial questions regarding how my loan was serviced and how balances were calculated. As I continued reviewing the available records, I identified numerous additional concerns requiring explanation, including : Significant unexplained increases in principal balance following the XXXX forbearance period. Numerous fees, corporate advances, and servicing charges that currently lack supporting documentation or sufficient explanation. Questions regarding the accounting used during my XXXX loan restructuring. Potential inconsistencies in the application of payments and changes in loan balances over time. Servicing records that do not currently allow me to independently reconcile the loan balance. Immediately following completion of the XXXX loan restructuring, the servicing rights to my mortgage were transferred to another mortgage servicer. Because of this transfer, I have experienced significant difficulty obtaining the complete servicing records necessary to verify the accuracy of the accounting performed by the prior servicer. I have formally requested the complete loan servicing file from origination through the present, including all payment histories, transaction ledgers, servicing notes, XXXX forbearance documentation, loan modification calculations, corporate advance documentation, escrow analyses, servicing transfer records, and other supporting documents necessary to perform a complete reconciliation of my mortgage account. At the time of filing this complaint, I am still awaiting those records. I am currently preparing a comprehensive forensic accounting reconstruction of my mortgage using the records available to me. This reconstruction includes a complete life-of-loan payment analysis, amortization reconstruction, escrow review, fee analysis, transaction reconciliation, and supporting documentation. The purpose of this reconstruction is to determine whether the servicing of my mortgage complied with applicable federal servicing requirements and whether all charges assessed against my loan were authorized and accurately calculated. Because the accounting discrepancies identified thus far are substantial, I am requesting that the CFPB review the servicing of my mortgage while my document request remains pending. Specifically, I respectfully request that the CFPB require the mortgage servicer to : XXXX. Provide a complete life-of-loan accounting from origination through the present. XXXX. Explain every increase in principal balance occurring during and after the XXXX forbearance period. XXXX. Produce documentation supporting every corporate advance, inspection fee, attorney fee, foreclosure-related charge, appraisal fee, property preservation charge, escrow adjustment, and any other amounts added to my account. XXXX. Provide all documentation supporting the VA loan restructuring calculations, including how each amount financed into the modified loan balance was determined. XXXX. Produce all XXXX forbearance records, agreements, internal servicing calculations, payment deferral calculations, and related communications. XXXX. Explain how all payments were applied throughout the life of the loan, including any unapplied or suspense account balances. XXXX. Provide documentation regarding the transfer of servicing, including the loan balance transmitted between servicers and the accounting supporting that transfer. At this time, I am not asking the CFPB to make conclusions regarding intent or misconduct. Consumer complaint narrative: Complaint Against Bank of America Regarding Permanent Account Closure Following Rental Scam Victimization I respectfully submit this complaint regarding Bank of Americas handling of my checking and savings accounts after I unknowingly became the victim of a rental scam. This complaint is not about asking Bank of America to honor a fraudulent check. I fully understand that the XXXX I received was ultimately fraudulent and that the Bank was correct not to credit those funds. Rather, my complaint concerns Bank of Americas decision to permanently terminate my banking relationship without first allowing me an opportunity to explain the circumstances, despite the fact that I acted responsibly by seeking guidance directly from Bank of America employees before taking any action. Background In XX/XX/year>, I listed my residential property for rent online. A prospective tenant contacted me and stated that they wished to rent my property. The individual offered to send a security deposit and rent payment to hold the property. On XX/XX/year>, I received an electronic check in the amount of {$4200.00}. Because I had never received an XXXX before, I did not attempt to deposit it myself. Instead, I visited the Bank of America branch in XXXX XXXX, California, specifically to seek guidance from a XXXXspeaking banker. I explained that this payment represented rent and a security deposit from a prospective tenant and that I had never handled an XXXX before. I showed the banker the original email containing the XXXX. The banker instructed me to print the XXXX and deposit it. I followed those instructions exactly. When the deposit failed, I did not attempt further deposits on my own. Instead, I visited a second Bank of America XXXX in XXXX XXXX I again explained that the payment represented rent and a security deposit for my rental property. I also explained that I was following instructions provided by another Bank of America employee. The banker reviewed the original email together with me and attempted another deposit. I later learned that the individual was operating a rental scam. Permanent Account Closure Approximately XXXX weeks later, Bank of America permanently closed my checking and savings accounts. When I contacted Bank of America, I was informed that : * I could never again open another checking or savings account with Bank of America. * The decision was final. * No additional appeal would be accepted. I fully understand that Bank of America has the right to manage account risk. However, I believe my circumstances deserved an individualized review because I was the victim of fraud rather than a participant in fraud. My Concerns I respectfully ask CFPB to review whether Bank of America handled my case fairly. Specifically : XXXX. I proactively sought guidance from Bank of America before depositing an unfamiliar payment instrument. XXXX. I fully disclosed the nature of the transaction to XXXX different Bank of America employees. XXXX. I showed the original email containing the XXXX to Bank employees. XXXX. I followed the instructions provided by Bank employees. XXXX. At no point was I warned that the transaction appeared fraudulent. XXXX. I was never contacted by Bank of America before the permanent account closure to provide an explanation or supporting documentation. XXXX. After my accounts were closed, Bank of America representatives repeatedly could not explain how my remaining account balance would be returned. XXXX. Bank representatives also could not clearly explain what had happened to another legitimate refund check that was in process. Resolution Requested I respectfully request that Bank of America : * conduct a meaningful review of the circumstances surrounding my case; * explain why a customer who sought professional guidance from Bank employees before taking any action was permanently prohibited from opening future deposit accounts; * provide a clear written explanation regarding the handling and return of my remaining lawful account balance ; * provide a clear explanation regarding the handling of my returned Capital One refund check ; * review whether the permanent restriction imposed on my ability to maintain deposit accounts appropriately reflects the facts of my case as the victim of a rental scam. I have supporting documentation, including communications with the scammer, deposit receipts, returned deposit notices, and a complete timeline of events. Thank you for your consideration.

Inconsistent account classification. XXXX reports this account 's Account Type as " COLLECTION. '' XXXX reports the identical account as " INSTALLMENT. '' A single account can not accurately be both. 2. Invalid account status code. XXXX reports the Account Status as " XXXX, '' which is not a valid or understandable status and does not reflect the true, paid status of this account. 3. Improper continuous re-reporting of collection status. My XXXX payment history shows this account coded as an active collection every single month from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, a continuous 31-month span. The furnisher 's own records show my date of first delinquency as XX/XX/XXXX and my last payment date as XX/XX/XXXX, with the account marked Paid as of XX/XX/XXXX. A single collection on a {$40.00} balance does not justify XXXX straight months of active collection reporting. 4. Underlying facts and failure to send required debt validation notice. The furnisher 's own record notes " Returned Check '' as additional information. This matches what happened : I submitted a payment directly to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, the original creditor, and that payment was not successfully processed. I did not receive any subsequent billing notices because I had relocated to a new address shortly after. I was not aware of any balance until it had already been placed for collection with XXXX, a third party I never had a direct relationship or account with. Once XXXX began collecting on this account, I never received a written validation notice from them as required under 15 U.S.C. Section 1692g, informing me of the debt, my right to dispute it, or my right to request verification before they proceeded with collection activity or credit reporting. XXXX was engaged in debt collection activity on this account without ever providing that legally required notice. 5. Inconsistent furnisher address information. The furnisher 's address is also listed differently across my credit report pulls, appearing with three different suite numbers on the same street, raising further concern about the accuracy of how this account is being maintained and reported. Both bureaus currently confirm this account 's payment status as Paid with a {$0.00} balance. Given the furnisher 's failure to provide required validation notice under 15 U.S.C. Section 1692g, combined with a conflicting account type, an invalid status code, a 31-month collection reporting pattern that does not match the account 's actual timeline, and inconsistent furnisher address information, I am requesting that this account be deleted from my credit reports at all three bureaus.

I have previously disputed this account ; however, the account continues to be furnished to consumer reporting agencies without correction. I dispute both the accuracy of the reported balance and my legal responsibility for the alleged debt. Pursuant to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( " FCRA '' ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ), a furnisher of information has a duty to conduct a reasonable investigation after receiving notice of a dispute from a consumer reporting agency, review all relevant information, and correct, modify, or delete information that is inaccurate or can not be verified. Additionally, 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) requires consumer reporting agencies to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of disputed information and delete information that can not be verified. Further, 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) requires consumer reporting agencies to maintain reasonable procedures to assure the maximum possible accuracy of the information contained in consumer reports. As a debt collector, IC System is prohibited under 15 U.S.C. 1692e, including 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ), from making any false, deceptive, or misleading representation regarding the character, amount, or legal status of an alleged debt. Additionally, 15 U.S.C. 1692f prohibits the use of unfair or unconscionable means to collect an alleged obligation. Pursuant to Regulation F, 12 C.F.R. 1006.18 and 1006.22, debt collectors are prohibited from using false, deceptive, misleading, unfair, or unconscionable practices in connection with the collection of a consumer debt. To date, IC System has failed to provide competent documentary evidence establishing : That I am legally obligated to pay the alleged {$150.00} balance ; The contractual basis supporting the amount being reported ; A complete itemization demonstrating how the alleged balance was calculated ; Documentation establishing that the information being furnished is complete, accurate, and legally enforceable. I further request that IC System provide written documentary proof establishing that it has the legal authority to collect this alleged debt, including documentation demonstrating whether it is collecting on behalf of the original creditor or otherwise possesses the legal right to enforce collection of this account. If IC System maintains that I owe this alleged debt, I request that it produce competent documentary evidence establishing both the validity of the alleged obligation and my legal responsibility for the amount being reported. Continued furnishing of information that can not be substantiated through a reasonable investigation may constitute inaccurate credit reporting under the Fair Credit Reporting Act and continues to cause consumer harm. Requested Resolution I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau require IC System , Inc. to : Conduct a reasonable investigation consistent with the requirements of the Fair Credit Reporting Act. Immediately cease furnishing this account to XXXX XXXX XXXX, and any other consumer reporting agency. Request deletion of every tradeline furnished by IC System concerning this alleged account because the information is disputed and, if it can not be substantiated through a reasonable investigation, should not continue to be reported. Provide written documentary proof establishing that IC System has the legal authority to collect this alleged debt. Provide written documentary proof establishing that I am legally responsible for the alleged debt. Provide a complete itemization explaining how the alleged {$150.00} balance was calculated. Provide documentation establishing the accuracy and legal basis of the information currently being furnished to consumer reporting agencies. If IC System can not substantiate this alleged debt through competent documentary evidence, immediately cease all collection activity, cease furnishing this account, and request deletion of every tradeline furnished to any consumer reporting agency. I reserve all rights afforded to me under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, Regulation F, and all other applicable federal and state consumer protection laws.

Consumer complaint narrative: I have been a USAA member since about XXXX ( checking ending XXXX, credit card ending XXXX ). This complaint concerns a sequence in which USAA ( XXXX ) enrolled my checking account in " Standard Overdraft '' by default, without any election by me ; ( XXXX ) sold me a 0 % promotional balance transfer while its own system held a standing autopay certain to destroy that balance, with no warning at the point of sale ; ( XXXX ) sent no advance alert before the autopay executed; and ( XXXX ) when I found it too late to stop, steered me into USAA 's own 16.39 % loan while never disclosing the no-cost option of letting the item return unpaid. USAA replaced its own 0 % obligation with its own 16.39 % loan. Timeline ( calls stated to my best recollection ; USAA 's recordings hold the verbatim record ) : - XX/XX/XXXX : Per USAA 's XX/XX/XXXX notices, Standard Overdraft was applied to eligible checking accounts by default. I made no election. Default enrollment without affirmative consent is contrary to Regulation XXXX 's opt-in framework ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) and at minimum unfair under XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX - XX/XX/XXXX : I created a " Statement Balance in Full '' autopay as a backstop. From XXXX I paid manually ; it rarely if ever executed. - XX/XX/XXXX : USAA approved a {$10000.00} balance transfer at 0 % APR through XX/XX/XXXX for a {$540.00} fee. No warning about the standing autopay appeared in the transfer flow. - XX/XX/XXXX : USAA emailed an advance alert for its own insurance autopay on the same profile. No alert preceded the credit card autopay. - XX/XX/XXXX : The autopay swept {$10000.00}, extinguishing the promotional balance. - XX/XX/XXXX : I discovered the sweep, too late to stop under USAA 's three-business-day window. On this and later calls, reps disclosed for the first time that Standard Overdraft was a default enrollment, said the sweep would " likely '' pay through it, and presented a USAA personal loan as the solution. No one disclosed the item could instead be returned unpaid, at no fee, with the balance intact. That omission and the steering into USAA 's own loan were deceptive and abusive under XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX. - XX/XX/XXXX : Relying on that guidance, I took loan no. XXXX ( {$10000.00} at 16.39 % ), sized to the sweep. I set the overdraft to Auto-Decline the day I learned it existed. - XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX XXXX : A USAA escalation rep promised on a recorded line ( case no. XXXX ) the payment would be " fixed and reversed. '' USAA 's written denial issued the same day, finding the transfer " valid '' because " initiated by an authorized user '', a question I never raised. USAA will likely respond that I " authorized '' the payment that ended the promotional terms. I authorized a standing autopay in XX/XX/XXXX as a backstop to my manually executed payments ; I did not authorize this rule, nearly a year and a half prior, with the intent to erase a 0 % balance I had just paid {$540.00} to establish. This is a problem USAA created and could have easily avoided with sufficient disclosure. It was mentioned by USAA representatives that the payment completed only because an overdraft setting I never elected, serviced it, and only because reps withheld the no-fee return that would have preserved the terms. The XXXX promise to " fix and reverse '' concedes a correction was warranted. I assert that the ambiguity of whether or not a payment will process through overdraft, at USAA 's sole discretion, is not a peripheral detail but a structural defect : because USAA reserves the pay-or-return decision to itself and does not disclose how that discretion will be exercised, its own representatives can not tell a member what will actually happen to a pending item. The most I was offered was that the sweep would " likely '' be paid, a guess about USAA 's own undisclosed decision, not advice a member can rely on. That uncertainty is not neutral ; it channels members away from no-cost outcomes USAA never discloses ( such as returning the transaction ) and toward the one certain option USAA places in front of them : a USAA-originated, high-interest loan. A program too indeterminate for the institution 's own staff to explain can not be one on which a member makes an informed decision. I therefore ask the Bureau to obtain the recorded calls, my overdraft enrollment records, and the transaction coding of the XX/XX/XXXX sweep, and to examine the default enrollment of these overdraft " protections, '' the selective failure to alert, the steering of a member from USAA 's own 0 % obligation into USAA 's own 16.39 % loan, and as the root of all of it whether an overdraft program whose discretion USAA will not disclose, and whose own representatives can not explain, is unfair and abusive under XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX.

Consumer complaint narrative: At approximately XXXX XXXX I was contacted by individuals falsely claiming to be the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in Florida. They stated my brother was detained and required immediate payment for alcohol classes and an ankle monitor as a condition of release. Based on this false representation of law enforcement authority and urgency, I sent funds. This was an impersonation scam. My brother had been arrested earlier that day for XXXX in XXXX XXXX, but the payment demand and details provided were fraudulent. I am filing a complaint regarding USAA Federal Savings Banks handling of my debit card fraud dispute. On XX/XX/year>, I was the victim of an impersonation scam. Scammers falsely claimed to be law enforcement and convinced me that I needed to send money immediately through XXXX XXXX to protect a family member. Believing the situation was legitimate, I used my USAA debit card to fund XXXX XXXX transactions. As soon as I realized I had been scammed, I immediately reported the fraud to USAA, filed a police report, and fully cooperated with their investigation. I provided all requested information and expected USAA to conduct a thorough investigation under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( Regulation E ). USAA denied my dispute, stating there was insufficient evidence that the merchandise or service was not received and that the transaction was successfully processed through the payment service. This response fails to address the actual issue. My dispute is not about merchandise or services that were not received. It is about unauthorized fraud resulting from a criminal impersonation scam that induced me to transfer funds under false pretenses. USAA appears to have focused only on whether XXXX XXXX successfully processed the payment instead of whether the transaction was induced by fraud and whether their investigation complied with Regulation E. Their denial letter provides little explanation of what evidence was reviewed or why the police report and other supporting documentation were not sufficient. I respectfully request that the CFPB review whether USAA : * Conducted a reasonable and good-faith investigation of my claim. * Properly applied the protections required under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E. * Correctly characterized my dispute instead of treating it as a simple merchant dispute involving goods or services. * Provide a detailed explanation of the evidence relied upon in denying my claim. I am requesting that USAA reopen my claim, conduct a complete and impartial investigation, and provide a detailed written explanation of its findings. If the investigation determines that my claim qualifies for protection under applicable law, I request reimbursement of the funds I lost as a result of this scam. I have been a USAA member in good standing and have always trusted the bank to protect its members from fraud. I am disappointed that, despite promptly reporting the scam and cooperating fully, my claim was denied based on reasoning that does not address the facts of my case. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint because American Coradius International is attempting to collect an alleged debt on behalf of XXXX that I dispute in its entirety. I do not believe this is a valid debt, and I believe it arose from an error in the way XXXX and its former credit card issuer handled a fraudulent transaction. In XX/XX/year>, a fraudulent transaction resulted in a temporary authorization hold of 120 on my XXXX XXXX XXXX. This was an authorization only. The transaction was never finalized or settled as a completed purchase. The merchant subsequently released and refunded the authorization, and I did not receive any goods or services from the transaction. Despite the transaction never becoming a valid completed charge, the matter was incorrectly processed through the dispute system associated with my XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX. As a result of that internal processing, XXXX ultimately debited approximately {$140.00} from my XXXX balance, creating a negative XXXX balance that I have consistently disputed. I do not believe this negative balance represents a legitimate debt because the underlying transaction was fraudulent and, to my understanding, never resulted in a valid charge for which I remained financially responsible. After discovering the negative balance, I repeatedly contacted both XXXX and XXXX XXXX which at the time was the issuer of the XXXX XXXX XXXX Rather than resolving the issue, each company directed me to the other. XXXX stated that XXXX was responsible for correcting the matter, while XXXX stated that XXXX was responsible. As a consumer, I was left without any meaningful resolution despite making numerous good-faith attempts to resolve the issue directly. XXXX XXXX has since resolved its involvement and is no longer attempting to collect any money from me. However, XXXX has continued to maintain that I owe the negative balance and has now referred the account to American Coradius International for collection. American Coradius has contacted me seeking payment of this alleged debt. I dispute the debt in its entirety because I do not believe any money is owed. I have requested that the debt be validated and that documentation be provided establishing the legal and factual basis for the alleged obligation, including documentation demonstrating how XXXX incurred a recoverable loss arising from a transaction that I believe was fraudulent and never resulted in a valid completed charge. From my perspective, I am now being subjected to collection efforts for a debt that should never have existed. I made repeated efforts to resolve the issue before it was referred to collections, but the underlying error was never corrected. Instead, the disputed balance was simply transferred to a third-party debt collector. I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate this matter and require XXXX XXXX XXXX to substantiate the alleged debt with competent documentation before continuing any collection efforts. If the debt can not be substantiated, I request that all collection activity cease, that the account be closed and returned to XXXX, and that no adverse information relating to this disputed debt be furnished to any consumer reporting agency. If any information has already been reported, I request that it be corrected or removed to accurately reflect that I dispute the validity of the alleged debt. I am not refusing to pay a legitimate debt. Rather, I am disputing that any valid debt exists in the first place and am requesting that XXXX XXXX demonstrate the legal basis for attempting to collect this amount.

Consumer complaint narrative: To Whom It May Concern : I am writing in response to your recent communication regarding the alleged debt referenced above. Pursuant to my rights under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g, I hereby request full validation of this debt. Under 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ), I have the right to dispute the validity of this debt and request verification. During the validation period, you are required to cease all collection activity until you provide the requested verification. Please provide the following information and documentation : 1. The exact amount of the alleged debt, including a complete itemization showing : The original principal amount Any interest, fees, or charges added The date of the last payment made The current creditor of record 2. The name and address of the original creditor to whom the debt was allegedly owed. 3. Proof that you are licensed to collect debt in this state, including your license number and the name/address of the licensing agency. 4. A copy of the original contract, agreement, or other document creating the alleged obligation, signed by me. 5. A complete payment history from the original creditor showing all payments, credits, and charges. 6. Proof that you have the legal authority and standing to collect this debt, including : The chain of assignment/ownership showing how the debt was transferred to you The date you acquired the debt The amount you paid for the debt ( if purchased ) 7. Verification that the statute of limitations has not expired on this debt. 8. Confirmation that this debt will be reported, or has been reported, to any credit reporting agency, and if so, the name of the agency and the date of reporting. ADDITIONAL LEGAL NOTICES : Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 16921692p : You are hereby notified that any false, deceptive, or misleading representation ; any harassment, oppression, or abuse ; or any unfair practice in connection with the collection of this debt will constitute a violation of federal law for which I may seek damages, attorney fees, and costs. Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. : If you report or have reported this debt to any credit reporting agency, you must report it accurately. Any inaccurate reporting may result in legal action. Telephone Consumer Protection Act ( TCPA ), 47 U.S.C. 227 : I do not consent to receiving calls or text messages to my cellular telephone using an automatic telephone dialing system or artificial/prerecorded voice. Any such calls are unauthorized. State Law Violations : Any violation of state debt collection laws may result in additional claims for damages. CEASE COMMUNICATION NOTICE : Until such time as you provide the requested validation, I demand that you : 1. Cease all collection activity on this account, including but not limited to phone calls, letters, emails, and text messages. 2. Refrain from reporting this debt to any credit reporting agency or, if already reported, immediately withdraw the tradeline pending validation. 3. Refrain from filing or threatening to file any lawsuit to collect this debt. 4. Refrain from garnishing wages, levying bank accounts, or placing liens on property. I am not acknowledging that I owe this debt. This letter is not an admission of liability. I reserve all rights under federal and state law. Please govern yourselves accordingly. Failure to provide proper validation or continued collection activity without validation will result in the filing of complaints with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), the state Attorney General, and may result in a civil lawsuit seeking statutory damages, actual damages, attorney fees, and costs. This request is time-sensitive. Please respond within 30 days of the date of this letter. Sincerely

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing a complaint against GoodLeap ( formerly LoanPal ) and XXXX XXXX for deceptive solar financing and XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX I was over XXXX at the time of the sale. XXXX XXXX assured me I would receive federal solar tax credits even though I told them I was on Social Security only and had no tax liability. They used this false promise to justify the financing structure. My loan payments were set at {$210.00} per month initially, increasing to {$300.00} per month when the tax credit I was promised did not materialize as I was never eligible for it. This is predatory financing. XXXX collapsed, and GoodLeap assumed the loan without providing any documentation of liability transfer. I am requesting investigation and relief, including loan correction or modification, due to misrepresentation at the point of sale and financial harm caused by deceptive practices. My solar purchase summary. My solar system contract was executed on XX/XX/XXXX. The following is a summary of how the transaction occurred. A salesman for the XXXX XXXX XXXX came to my door about a month prior to the purchase. He made multiple trips to my home to try and convince me to make the purchase of this solar system. The salesperson was well aware of my situation as myself and my husband lived solely on Social Security. As we were on a very limited income, this decision was very difficult for me to make. My husband had suffered a XXXX XXXX in XXXX and was totally XXXX until his death in XXXX. Although the salesperson knew my financial situation, he assured me over and over that the tax credits would pay so much of the cost of the solar system. This, in my mind, ultimately made me feel that the purchase was worth it. He actually went as far as to bring a second individual to my home that he presented as his supervisor to assure me that we would be eligible for all of the tax credits and explain how much we would get per year to assist in this purchase. They just made it sound like such a good deal to me. Once the paperwork was prepared they returned to present the paperwork to me. At the time I had some vision issues due to cataracts, which have since been corrected. I was unable to read the fine print so they went over it page by page with me and read the contract terms to me. At the time I did not realize that the contract was written to XXXX XXXX, my husband, and was all electronically signed. I don't understand how that happened because XXXX XXXX was XXXX XXXX XXXX and unable to make any decisions of his own. I can only assume they used him because he probably had better credit or enough credit to make this transaction happen but it would have been impossible for XXXX XXXX to have approved this transaction. I did not realize this until much later, when the inverter failed and needed to be replaced. I needed to contact them and they would not even talk to me because I was not the person supposedly that made this transaction. That's how I became aware that XXXX XXXX 's signature was used to make the purchase. Ultimately I feel I was misled, lied to, and taken advantage of. These people knew my husband and I were on a fixed income and had no tax liability so they absolutely knew we were never going to be able to get the tax credits that were promised to us. I feel it's very unfortunate that companies like this will prey on senior citizens. Early this year I saw online that there were companies and legal organizations to assist you with matters like this. I contacted one and they advised me to get as much paperwork as I could from Good Leap and forward it to them for review. They told me I had a very good case but they wanted {$2000.00} down and wanted me to make payments XXXX for the next 12 to 14 months in order to resolve this. As my husband passed in XXXX, I had lost one of the social security checks and it is even more of a challenge today to make ends meet on a monthly basis. There was no way that I could afford to pay this company to resolve the matter for me. As of today I even rely on food assistance to make ends meet on a monthly basis. I continue to research and found some people who had posted online that you could do this yourself so this is where I am at today and I am forwarding this to you for your consideration. I would like to thank you in advance for any resolution that you may be able to offer. Attached are the scans of the original purchase and also the PDFs that I received from Good Leap earlier this year.

There are a total of 3 dates of service involved - XX/XX/year>, XX/XX/year>XXXX and XX/XX/year>. The collection attorney also refuses to settle the 2 dates of service I have offered to pay since I will not also pay for the 3rd as I do not agree to paying a debt that is not legally valid. Consumer complaint narrative: EXETER FINANCE LLC is reporting a vehicle-finance account in my name as a charge-off. I dispute the accuracy and completeness of this account and request that the charge-off and related account information be deleted unless Exeter can fully verify the obligation through reliable evidence. Exeter Finance LLC 's continued reporting of this account as a charge-off has caused substantial and ongoing financial harm. Because of this reporting, I have been denied credit, my credit score has declined, and my ability to obtain financing and secure housing has been negatively affected. The inaccurate reporting has made it difficult for me to move because landlords and lenders review my credit history when evaluating rental and financing applications. This disputed account has damaged my financial reputation and continues to interfere with my ability to obtain affordable credit, housing, and other financial opportunities. I do not dispute this account merely because the matter is in arbitration. I dispute the underlying liability itself. I have consistently informed Exeter that I did not knowingly receive, review, authorize, or electronically sign the Retail Installment Sales Contract that Exeter claims created this debt. I also dispute the alleged electronic signatures, Exeters assignment and ownership rights, the claimed security interest and lien, the reported balance, and Exeters authority to report the account as a valid debt. The alleged contract was not presented to me during my XX/XX/year>XXXX dealership visit. I first received the disputed Retail Installment Sales Contract later with documents described as second copies. The document contains alleged electronic signatures that I do not recognize as electronic acts I knowingly performed or authorized. Exeter has not provided a complete electronic-signature audit trail showing the device, authentication method, signing session, timestamps, user information, or other reliable evidence proving that I signed the specific contract it reports. The account also arises from a vehicle transaction involving disputed dates, financing disclosures, title records, lien information, co-buyer representations, and assignment rights. These issues remain part of a pending arbitration involving Exeter Finance LLC and XXXX XXXX XXXX. The arbitrator denied disposition of the principal issues involving the underlying transaction, leaving those matters for an evidentiary hearing. When I requested the Truth in Lending disclosure, XXXX provided the worksheet and represented it as the disclosure. It created my understanding of the transaction. '' Despite receiving repeated notice that I dispute owing Exeter any money under the alleged contract, Exeter continued reporting the account and has now changed the status to a charge-off. Reporting the account as a valid charged-off obligation presents the disputed debt as established even though Exeter has not provided sufficient evidence that I knowingly entered the alleged contract or that Exeter obtained an enforceable assignment and security interest. I request that the CFPB require Exeter to conduct a real and reasonable investigation rather than merely confirm the information through its own internal account records. Exeter should review the original transaction evidence, electronic-signature records, all versions of the contract and title documents, the complete chain of assignment, my prior written disputes, and the pending arbitration record.

I am requesting that Vance & Huffman conduct a complete investigation using the original application, identity-verification records, electronic authorization records , loan-disbursement records, bank-account information, payment history, and address records. I have attached a copy of the written dispute I sent to Vance & Huffman, along with the companys XX/XX/year>XXXX response and a screenshot showing the collection on my credit report. Consumer complaint narrative: CFPB Complaint Company : Citibank , N.A . Product : Credit Card Issue : Billing Dispute Investigation Complaint I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau review Citibanks handling of my billing dispute concerning defective merchandise purchased with my Citibank credit card. This complaint is not about whether I authorized the purchase. I acknowledge that I made the purchase and that the charge itself is valid. This complaint concerns whether Citibank conducted a reasonable investigation into my dispute involving defective merchandise that failed to perform its intended function as advertised, and whether Citibank fairly considered all relevant evidence before denying my claim. Background On XX/XX/year>, I purchased a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX for {$6900.00}. The printer was delivered on XX/XX/year>. Because the equipment required assembly, stand installation, software installation, ink and film loading, and printer configuration before operation, setup took several days to complete. The printers first production print occurred on XX/XX/year>. During its first operational use, the printer failed to perform as intended. The XXXX XXXX transfer would not properly release from the B-film or adhere correctly to multiple application surfaces, resulting in unusable finished products. The defect was discovered during the printers initial operational use. Extensive Efforts to Resolve the Problem Before requesting a refund or filing a dispute, I made every reasonable effort to work directly with the merchant to resolve the issue. Between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/year>, I participated in numerous troubleshooting sessions with XXXX technical support team. These efforts included : Multiple remote access sessions in which XXXX technicians connected directly to my computer. Numerous adjustments to printer settings by XXXX technicians. Submission of photographs and videos demonstrating the defect. A final troubleshooting session lasting approximately XXXX hours. Despite these extensive efforts, the printer never produced a usable result. Only after these troubleshooting efforts failed did I request authorization to return the printer for a full refund. This was not buyers remorse or a change of mind. I invested significant time attempting to make the printer function before requesting authorization to return it. Merchant Admissions On XX/XX/year>, XXXX acknowledged in writing : The B-film adhesion/release issue you are experiencing is not a known problem reported by other users, indicating that the problem exists only in your device and is not a systemic issue with the printer model itself. In the same communication, XXXX further acknowledged : You have conducted extensive remote troubleshooting with our technical team, and unfortunately, these efforts have not been able to resolve your issue. These written admissions establish that : XXXX knew exactly what defect was being reported. XXXX acknowledged the issue appeared unique to my specific printer. XXXX acknowledged that extensive troubleshooting had already occurred. XXXX acknowledged that those troubleshooting efforts had failed. Return Request After troubleshooting proved unsuccessful, I requested authorization to return the defective printer for a full refund. A return for a full refund was never authorized. Instead, XXXX repeatedly requested additional troubleshooting. Months later, after Citibank contacted XXXX regarding my dispute, XXXX suggested that I ship the printer back. However, XXXX did not commit in writing to : providing a full refund ; paying return shipping ; specifying inspection timeframes ; or explaining the conditions under which a refund would actually be issued. Had XXXX accepted the return of the defective printer for a full refund when requested, this dispute would never have been necessary. Concerns Regarding Citibanks Investigation Throughout the dispute process, I submitted documentation including : a detailed timeline, photographs demonstrating the defect, merchant correspondence, documentation of extensive troubleshooting, and XXXX written acknowledgements regarding the defect. I also emailed video evidence showing the printers failure during troubleshooting. After being told the videos could not be opened, I asked how that evidence could be submitted, but I did not receive instructions for submitting the videos. Despite this documentation, Citibank denied the dispute. The denial letters raise several concerns. One determination stated that Citibank was unable to identify or determine that a billing error had occurred. When I questioned that determination, Citibank acknowledged that the dispute had been coded incorrectly and reopened the dispute. The second denial stated that I had possessed the merchandise for an extended period before discovering the defect. However, the documented timeline shows : XX/XX/XXXX XXXX received. XX/XX/XXXX First operational use. XX/XX/XXXX Defect discovered during first use. XX/XX/XXXX Return requested after multiple unsuccessful troubleshooting sessions. This timeline is not consistent with the conclusion that the defect was discovered only after an extended period of ownership. Additionally, Citibanks XXXX XXXX XXXXXX/XX/year> determination states : We have investigated your dispute involving a service ( s ) which was not performed. Since the merchant was willing to provide the service ( s ), we are unable to assist you further. My dispute did not involve services that were not performed. My dispute concerned defective merchandise that failed to perform its intended function as advertised. This language raises a concern that the dispute may not have been investigated under the correct dispute category. Request for CFPB Review I respectfully request that the CFPB review whether Citibank conducted a reasonable investigation by determining : Whether the dispute was investigated under the correct dispute category. Whether Citibank considered the complete timeline demonstrating that the defect was discovered during the printers first operational use. Whether Citibank considered XXXX written admissions acknowledging both the defect and unsuccessful troubleshooting. Whether Citibank evaluated whether XXXX ever actually offered to accept the return of the printer for a full refund. Whether Citibanks conclusions were supported by the evidence contained within the dispute file. I am not asking the CFPB to determine whether the printer is defective. Rather, I respectfully request that the CFPB review whether Citibank fulfilled its obligation to conduct a fair, complete, and reasonable investigation of my billing dispute.

Consumer complaint narrative: After reviewing my updated consumer credit reports, I identified that several previously disputed items continue to remain on my credit files despite my prior requests for removal. I am submitting this 4th follow-up removal request because inaccurate, unverifiable, and unauthorized information continues to be reported by Experian , Equifax, and TransUnion without proper validation. I am requesting CFPB assistance because these items have not been properly investigated or removed, even though they can not be verified as accurate. I am requesting complete removal and deletion only, not correction, modification, or updating, because these accounts and inquiries remain improperly reported and should not continue appearing on my consumer reports. The continued reporting of this information violates my rights under FCRA 611 ( a ) 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ), which requires consumer reporting agencies to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of disputed information, and FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), which requires furnishers to report accurate and complete information. The reporting of inaccurate delinquency information also violates FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 5 ), and the failure to maintain reasonable procedures to ensure maximum possible accuracy violates FCRA 607 ( b ) 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ). For accounts reporting balances exceeding {$600.00}, no sufficient documentation has been provided to establish the validity of the alleged debt, including complete account records, payment history, ownership verification, or applicable cancellation of debt documentation such as a 1099-C. The remaining disputed charge-off accounts include XXXX XXXX XXXX account XXXX in XXXX with a balance of {$6600.00} reported by Experian , XXXX XXXX XXXX account ending in XXXX with a balance of {$6600.00} reported by Equifax, and XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX account ending in XXXX with a balance of {$6600.00} reported by TransUnion. These accounts continue to be reported as charge-offs without sufficient evidence proving the accuracy of the balances, account history, payment records, ownership, or Date of First Delinquency. The continued reporting of these accounts violates FCRA 611 ( a ) 15 U.S.C. 1681i ( a ) and FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 5 ) because disputed information must be properly verified before remaining on a consumer report. The furnishers have also failed to comply with FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) because the information being furnished has not been proven accurate or complete, and the credit reporting agencies have failed to maintain maximum possible accuracy as required by FCRA 607 ( b ) 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ). I am also disputing unauthorized inquiries that remain on my consumer reports. My Experian report contains disputed inquiries from XXXX dated XX/XX/XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX dated XX/XX/XXXX, and XXXXXXXX XXXX dated XX/XX/XXXX. My Equifax report contains disputed inquiries from XXXX XXXX dated XX/XX/XXXX and XXXX dated XX/XX/XXXX. I do not recognize these inquiries, did not authorize these companies to access my consumer report, and have not been provided documentation showing a valid permissible purpose or written authorization. These inquiries violate FCRA 604 ( a ) 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( a ), which requires a permissible purpose before accessing consumer report information, and FCRA 604 ( f ) 15 U.S.C. 1681b ( f ), which prohibits obtaining or using a consumer report without a lawful purpose. Additionally, improper access or unauthorized obtaining of consumer report information may violate FCRA 619 15 U.S.C. 1681q. Despite my previous disputes and follow-up requests, these charge-off accounts and inquiries remain on my credit reports without proper verification. I am requesting CFPB assistance in requiring Experian , Equifax, and TransUnion to permanently remove all remaining disputed charge-off accounts and unauthorized inquiries listed above because they are inaccurate, unverifiable, and improperly reported.

Consumer complaint narrative: CRITICAL NOTICE TO INVESTIGATOR AND RESPONDENT : The CFPB electronic portal forces consumers to select from a restrictive list of predefined, automated dropdown categories to submit a form. The consumer has selected the closest available structural option ( " Dispute the Amount '' ) under protest solely to bypass portal formatting constraints.This submission is made strictly as a dispute regarding structural non-compliance, lack of statutory chain of title, and material misrepresentations by the collector. This filing does not constitute a validation of liability, an admission or acknowledgment of any alleged debt instrument, or a waiver of any consumer rights under federal or state law. The consumer reserves all rights to contest the existence, ownership, validity, and enforceability of the alleged balance in its entirety. I am submitting this formal complaint against Second Alliance , Inc. ( XXXX XXXX, CA ) for explicit violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), the Oregon Unlawful Debt Collection Practices Act ( OUDCPA ), and the California Rosenthal Act. The agency is engaging in unlawful continued collection activities and utilizing material misrepresentations to pressure me into an unsafe refinancing agreement. 1. Failure to Provide Mandatory Chain of Title Following an initial communication, Second Alliance , Inc. sent a validation packet containing only an underlying student loan contract executed with XXXX Bank. On XXXX XXXX XXXX, I exercised my rights under ORS 646A.670 and sent a formal statutory dispute noticing the deficiency. I demanded physical business recordssuch as an assignment agreement or bill of saleproving a clear, unbroken chain of ownership from the original creditor ( XXXX Bank ) to the current alleged owner. Second Alliance , Inc. failed to produce any physical transfer documentation. 2. False, Deceptive, and Contradictory Ownership Narrative Instead of pausing collection efforts to compile the statutory evidence, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX sent a response letter containing a blatant factual and legal impossibility. The letter explicitly states : " The owner and loan holder is and has always been XXXX student loan. XXXX was the originating lender. '' Under 15 U.S.C. 1692e and Cal. Civ. Code 1788.17, debt collectors are strictly prohibited from using false or misleading representations regarding the character or legal status of a debt. An originating lender is, by definition, the first legal owner and holder of a signed promissory note. Therefore, Edly could not have " always '' been the holder. Furthermore, independent credit reporting data directly refutes the agency 's claim. The consumer 's credit profile shows the loan was held under " XXXX '' ( XXXX Bank ) until XX/XX/scrub>XXXX XXXX, moved to " XXXX '' for one month, and was explicitly marked " Transferred to another lender '' in XX/XX/scrub>XXXX XXXX This independent credit data proves that the loan has undergone multiple structural assignments and transfers, making the agency 's written claim of continuous, unbroken ownership a patently false misrepresentation designed to obscure a missing chain of title. 3. Unlawful Continued Collections and Refinancing Solicitation While my statutory validation request remained pending and unfulfilled, Second Alliance , Inc. actively continued collection efforts by attempting to solicit a {$350.00} voluntary payment to " re-age '' the loan. Furthermore, they used this deceptive ownership narrative to push a high-pressure solicitation to " refinance '' the debt through a partner lender. Under Oregon law ( ORS 646.639 ) and California 's Rosenthal Act ( Cal. Civ. Code 1788.17 ), a debt collector must completely cease and freeze all collection efforts upon receiving a consumer dispute until accurate validation is provided. Attempting to maneuver a consumer out of a highly disputable contract with missing ownership records and into a brand-new, refinanced loan agreement before validating the debt constitutes an unfair, deceptive, and abusive collection practice.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding Freedom Mortgage Corporations handling of my FHA mortgage loss-mitigation application, its inaccurate or misleading characterization of my first Trial Payment Plan, its failure to acknowledge my successful completion of a second Trial Payment Plan, and its XX/XX/XXXX denial of substantially all home-retention options. On XX/XX/XXXX, Freedom approved me for a Standalone Loan Modification subject to a three-month Trial Payment Plan. The plan required payments of {$2800.00} for XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. I accepted the plan and made the first XXXX required payments, totaling {$5600.00}. XXXX XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX mortgage statements reflect those payments. On XX/XX/XXXX, before the third payment was due, I wrote to Freedom requesting that the anticipated permanent modification be structured at a sustainable payment level. I expressly stated : I want to emphasize that I am fully committed to completing the Trial Period Plan in good faith and maintaining the loan going forward. I did not state that I was rejecting mortgage assistance, abandoning the XXXX XXXX XXXX, or refusing to comply with its terms. Nevertheless, on XX/XX/XXXX, Freedom issued a letter stating that the program was not completed because of Borrower Rejected Current Workout. That characterization was inaccurate or, at minimum, materially misleading. My XX/XX/XXXX letter asked Freedom to consider an affordable permanent structure and expressly reaffirmed my commitment to the loss-mitigation process. On the same date ( XX/XX/XXXX ), Freedom separately acknowledged my submission as a facially complete loss-mitigation application and stated that it would review me for all possible workout options. After reevaluating my application, Freedom issued a second Trial Payment Plan dated XX/XX/XXXX. That plan required XXXX monthly payments of {$2700.00} for XXXX, XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. I timely made all three payments under the second plan, totaling {$8300.00}. Freedom accepted the payments and, after I completed the plan, issued a permanent loan-modification approval dated XX/XX/XXXX. The proposed permanent modification required an estimated total monthly payment of {$2700.00}, including {$1300.00} in principal and interest and {$1300.00} in escrow. Because the payment was not sustainable, I submitted a written request on XX/XX/XXXX asking Freedom to reevaluate me for the FHA Payment Supplement, Partial Claim, Combination Loan Modification and Partial Claim, principal deferment, escrow review, and all other available FHA home-retention options. Freedom acknowledged that the XX/XX/XXXX request was a facially complete loss-mitigation application and stated that it would review me for all possible workout options. Nevertheless, Freedom issued a XX/XX/XXXX denial stating, among other things : Your loan has exceeded the limit for defaulted trial plans ; and You have failed to remit payments in accordance with the forbearance or trial plan you were approved for. The denial does not identify which XXXX XXXX XXXX Freedom claims was defaulted. It does not identify any particular missed payment, due date, or amount. It also fails to distinguish the incomplete first Trial Payment Plan from the second Trial Payment Plan that I successfully completed. The statement that I failed to remit payments under an approved trial plan is false as applied to the second plan. I made all three required payments, Freedom accepted them, and Freedom issued a permanent modification approval after the plan was completed. Freedoms XXXX denial is therefore inconsistent with its own payment records and its XX/XX/XXXX permanent-modification approval. Across both XXXX XXXX XXXX, I paid Freedom a total of {$14000.00}. I have requested a complete accounting showing how each payment was received, held, applied, or credited. I have also requested an explanation of the suspense and unapplied funds reflected on the mortgage statements and how those funds were treated when Freedom calculated the proposed modified principal balance. Freedom has not provided a transaction-level accounting demonstrating that the full {$14000.00} was properly credited once and that no amount was omitted, duplicated, misapplied, or added to the modified balance without a corresponding credit. I submitted a timely formal appeal to Freedom Mortgage on XX/XX/XXXX. A complete copy of that appeal, together with supporting Exhibits XXXX through XXXX, is attached to this CFPB complaint. Resolution Requested I request that Freedom Mortgage be required to : Conduct an independent review of its XX/XX/XXXX denial ; Correct the XX/XX/XXXX Borrower Rejected Current Workout characterization to reflect that I requested affordable permanent terms and did not reject mortgage assistance ; Identify every Trial Payment Plan that Freedom counts as defaulted, including the date, payment, amount, internal disposition, and FHA servicing code associated with each alleged default ; Confirm in writing that I successfully completed the XX/XX/XXXX Trial Payment Plan by making all three required payments totaling {$8300.00} ; Correct any internal or FHA record identifying the successfully completed second Trial Payment Plan as failed, rejected, withdrawn, or otherwise unsuccessful ; Explain the specific FHA XXXX under which an earlier incomplete Trial Payment Plan allegedly bars reconsideration after Freedom approved and I successfully completed a subsequent plan ; Reevaluate me for the FHA XXXX XXXX, Standalone Partial Claim, Combination Loan Modification and Partial Claim, principal deferment, and all other available FHA home-retention options ; Provide the calculations used for each option, including the unpaid principal balance, XXXX XXXX, delinquency cure amount, targeted principal-and-interest payment, interest rate, resulting payment, and precise basis for approval or denial ; Provide a complete accounting of all XXXX Trial Payment Plan payments totaling {$14000.00}, including the date received, amount applied, payment period credited, amount placed in suspense, amount remaining unapplied, and treatment of those funds in the proposed modified balance ; Correct any payment-history, loss-mitigation, or trial-plan coding errors ; Refrain from advancing foreclosure activity while my timely appeal and this servicing dispute remain under review; and If Freedom maintains that no FHA home-retention option is available, provide a fully itemized XXXX amount and the XXXX reasonable repayment arrangement available. I remain willing to make a sustainable mortgage payment and retain the property. I am not seeking to avoid my mortgage obligation. I am requesting accurate servicing records, a complete accounting of my payments, and a fair evaluation under the applicable FHA loss-mitigation requirements. Cordially, XXXX XXXX XXXX

My household experienced a temporary financial hardship related to a severe Tennessee winter storm and declared disaster. My XXXX mortgage was placed into a disaster-related forbearance. As the forbearance approached its end, I remained in frequent contact with ServiceMac and sought an extension because the financial effects of the disaster had not fully resolved. On XX/XX/year>, I called ServiceMac and spoke with a representative for approximately XXXX minutes. During that call, I was specifically advised not to make a mortgage payment until a decision was made on my pending appeal/review. I was told more than once that the time spent waiting for the review would not be held against me and that ServiceMac would not report late payments, assess late fees, or pursue foreclosure while the matter remained under review. I relied on those representations. On the same date, I submitted a written reconsideration request specifically seeking reconsideration of the denial of my disaster forbearance extension. ServiceMac 's portal confirms that the document was submitted on XX/XX/XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, ServiceMac sent me written confirmation that it had received and was reviewing additional items I submitted. Throughout this period, ServiceMac repeatedly represented in writing that my request remained under active review. I received written communications dated XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX stating that ServiceMac was still actively working on my loss mitigation loan request, was diligently reviewing all the necessary details, and would keep me updated regarding progress. During prior telephone communications, I was also told that denial notices reflecting denied loss mitigation options were issued because I was not eligible for those options while my forbearance remained active and that my account would be reassessed after the forbearance ended. On XX/XX/year>, I made multiple calls to ServiceMac seeking clarification and resolution. During those calls, ServiceMac informed me that I had been reassessed for loss mitigation and denied because I had not made a sufficient number of mortgage payments between origination and the beginning of my disaster forbearance. This stated basis for denial appears directly inconsistent with the FHA Single Family Housing Policy Handbook XXXX, Update XXXX, Section XXXX ( D ), page XXXX. If the applicable comparison does not direct a Standalone Loan Modification and the arrearage is within available Partial Claim funds, the waterfall states to offer the borrower a Standalone Partial Claim.
